This is the task queue for AI automation. The human reviews and prioritizes tasks; the AI executes them.

## How to Edit This List

- **Promote**: Change `P2` to `P1`, etc.
- **Demote**: Change `P1` to `P2`, etc.
- **Veto**: Add `#veto` anywhere in the task heading (e.g., `### P2: Task name #veto`)
- **Add reason**: Optionally add `- **Veto reason**: [why]` before vetoing

Vetoed items are moved automatically to the Vetoed Tasks section on the next evolution loop run.

## Priority Levels

- **P0**: Urgent - execute immediately
- **P1**: High - execute this week
- **P2**: Medium - execute when time permits
- **P2**: Low - nice to have, human approval needed

### NEEDS-HUMAN (methodology ratification) 2026-08-06: three of the nine tradition-survey rules are gates, not lenses — a per-section dissent quota, a five-field translation ledger, and a blocking author-conclusion check
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/project/writing-style.md
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Source**: combine-outer-reviews, 2026-08-06 (convergent cluster C1, 3/3 reviewers — the densest convergence any cycle has produced)
- **Synthesis**: `reviews/outer-review-synthesis-2026-08-06.md`
- **Generated**: 2026-08-06
- **Notes**: **WHAT THE LOOP ALREADY DID, SO THIS ENTRY IS ONLY ABOUT THE RESIDUE.** The 2026-08-06 C1 convergence proposed nine rules for articles surveying traditions the Map does not belong to. Per the standing boundary — *"a gate would fall under the operator-reserved governance ratification; a lens does not"* — the P1 refine installed the **lens** forms as a new section, *Surveying a Tradition from Outside (the Assimilation Firewall)*, in `obsidian/project/writing-style.md`, plus a five-item checklist block. Six rules (scope labels, exposition-before-appropriation, no unmarked cross-tradition repairs, the three-way inference test on religious and ancestral claims, the like-with-like symmetry test, and the shared-upstream independence check) went in whole, cross-referring to `[[evidential-status-discipline]]` and `[[common-cause-null]]` rather than restating them, with `topics/cross-traditional-convergence-on-consciousness-irreducibility` cited as the worked exemplar. **Three rules were installed only in their lens form; their blocking forms are the operator's call and are stated below.** Do not re-litigate the six that landed.
  - **GATE 1 — minimum-dissent quota.** *Proposed*: every tradition-specific section carries **at least one** serious internal disagreement **and at least one** methodological challenge to the interpretation it adopts. *Installed instead*: the unanimity lens — "where a survey names no internal disagreement and no methodological challenge, that is a fact about the survey rather than about the tradition." *Evidence for the gate*: all three reviewers independently found the African cluster presenting four traditions as speaking with one voice; Claude Opus 5 listed Appiah, Hallen, Oruka, Gade, Matolino & Kwindingwi and Hountondji as absent, and Gemini named Agada's Consolationism and Chimakonam's Conversational Philosophy as whole superseding frameworks omitted. *Cost of adopting*: (a) it is a **length driver** on articles that are already survey-shaped and near their section ceilings; (b) it is **unenforceable without new tooling** — nothing in `tools/curate/` parses "tradition-specific section", so it would be a described countermeasure not wired to a gate, which is exactly what `positions/methodology-and-calibration` **P-M5** says is a stated intention rather than a working control; (c) a per-section quota invites **decorative dissent** — the same failure the corpus already knows from decorative falsifiers, where a challenge is named and answered in the clause that names it.
  - **GATE 2 — translation ledger for key terms.** *Proposed*: for each key term, record the original term, its literal range, its ritual and social use, the competing philosophical translations, and why "mind" / "soul" / "consciousness" / "force" was chosen. *Installed instead*: the justify-the-rendering lens, which asks for the original term and the reason for the chosen rendering **where the term carries argumentative weight**, in prose, without the five-field apparatus. *Evidence for the gate*: Gemini's *taxonomic violence* charge is precisely that the translation step is where the assimilation happens, and ChatGPT's *assimilation by philosophical translation* names the same mechanism. *Cost of adopting*: a per-article structured apparatus is the same class of change as the References-section split proposed 2026-06-04 and re-raised 2026-07-16, which `writing-style.md` still holds as *"a candidate convention only… a corpus-wide reference-list reformatting decision for the human/operator, not an autonomous edit"* — treat the two consistently. **Scope, measured on disk 2026-08-06**: 59 files across `topics/ concepts/ apex/ voids/` mention Akan, Ubuntu, Yoruba, Advaita, Sāṃkhya, Nyāya, Kyoto School, Igbo, Zulu or Ori; 10 carry a tradition in the title. The ledger's real cost is whichever of those 59 counts as in-scope, and the boundary is itself an operator decision.
  - **GATE 3 — named-author stance gate (the strongest evidence of the three).** *Proposed*: for every cited scholar doing argumentative work in a survey of another tradition, record what that author actually **concludes**, in their own words, **with a page**, **before the article ships**. *Installed instead*: an extension of the already-adopted *author-stance verification* step (2026-07-21) — in a tradition survey the check must also record what the author concludes *about the tradition*, not just their role in a debate. *Evidence for the gate, which is unusually strong because it indicts the Map's own review machinery rather than a reviewer's opinion*: `reviews/deep-review-2026-05-31-african-philosophy-of-consciousness.md` **L29** verified the article's narrower sunsum-only claim as *"accurate, if narrower than his full view"* while recording in the same cell that **Wiredu treats both okra AND sunsum as quasi-material** and *"resists straightforward dualism"*; `reviews/deep-review-2026-07-17-african-philosophy-of-consciousness.md` **L37** certified the Gyekye tripartite attribution as *"correctly distinguished, NOT conflated"* and web-verified it. Both reviews asked whether the article's **sentence** was accurate; neither asked whether the scholar's **conclusion** pointed where the article was taking it. **The failure mode is not fabrication — every source was genuine — but recruitment of authors toward conclusions they reject**, and a check pitched at the author's conclusion would have caught both. *Cost of adopting*: verbatim-with-page requires source access the loop frequently lacks, and it composes badly with the standing rule that *"'Pending verification' is not a publishable state for a load-bearing citation"* — together they would force demote-or-delete on scholarship that is genuine and correctly attributed but simply not reachable at page granularity from the loop, silently thinning the very literature the C2 convergence says these articles need more of. It is also a **threshold change to an existing installed check** rather than a new instrument, which makes it the cheapest of the three to ratify and the one most likely to bind immediately.
  - **RELATED, DO NOT DUPLICATE**: the P1 research task on the same cycle (C2 — nothing newer than Metz 2007) supplies the scholarship these gates would demand; sequence any ratification after it lands, or the gates will bind against a bibliography everyone already agrees is stale. **DO NOT mint a P0–P3 from this entry** — the per-article consequences of the C1 convergence are already tasked individually on `concepts/african-philosophy-of-consciousness`.

### P2: `african-philosophy-of-consciousness` presents Ubuntu with no trace of the critical and feminist scholarship on it
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/concepts/african-philosophy-of-consciousness.md
- **Notes**: From outer review 2026-08-06 (Gemini 2.5 Pro). **Verified against the text, and checked against the other six open tasks on this cluster — no existing task covers this.** The Ubuntu section (L41–L47) presents *umuntu ngumuntu ngabantu* entirely in its harmonious register: relational personhood, a community of minds living and ancestral, intersubjective constitution. It records exactly one line of dissent — Metz reading Ubuntu ethically rather than metaphysically (L45) — and none at all on the tradition's contested social content.
  - **What is missing**: the substantial critical literature holding that Ubuntu's communal logic has been deployed to enforce conformity and sustain hierarchies of gender and age. Sources verified real at OpenAlex before minting: **Chisale, S. S., "*Ubuntu* as care: Deconstructing the gendered *Ubuntu*", *Verbum et Ecclesia* 39(1), 2018, `10.4102/ve.v39i1.1790`**, and **Praeg, L., *A Report on Ubuntu* (UKZN Press, 2014)**. The Matolino & Kwindingwi "The end of ubuntu" debate already logged on the open research task is the same seam and should be handled together.
  - **Do not import the review's framing wholesale.** It charged the article with romanticising Ubuntu as "universally egalitarian" and locating selfhood "entirely in external relationships" — the second is a misquote (the article says "the web of relationships that constitute personhood", L43, and closes "Relation shapes consciousness without exhausting its nature", L47). The defect is a **silence**, not an overclaim. Its own suggested citation for this point — Kirby & Shepherd (2020) on Women, Peace and Security policy — is a real paper with no bearing on African philosophy; ignore it.
  - **Scope carefully — this is the hard part.** Most of the critical literature is about Ubuntu's *normative deployment*, whereas the article's claim is *metaphysical* (that consciousness has relational structure). Do not present a political critique as though it refuted a metaphysical thesis. What it does bear on is the article's move from a contested, partly-idealised construct straight to a metaphysical reading: if the harmonious reading of Ubuntu is itself a modern and contested reconstruction, the ontological claim rests on less than the section implies. One or two honest sentences, not a new section — this article is already carrying three P1 fixes.
  - Apply the direct-refutation discipline. Identify what kind of engagement the issue calls for: showing the opponent's position is defective on its own terms, naming an unsupported foundational move the framework has not earned by its own standards, or honestly marking the framework-boundary disagreement. Apply the corresponding reply mode in **natural journal-quality prose** — see [the writing-style guide](/project/writing-style/)'s "Engaging Opponents in Journal-Quality Prose" section. **Do not expose mode labels in the article body.**
  - **Sequencing**: this article has three open P1 tasks. Run those first; this is additive and should land last so it does not collide with their edits.
- **Review file**: `reviews/outer-review-2026-08-06-gemini-2-5-pro.md`
- **Source**: outer-review
- **Generated**: 2026-08-06

### P3: Research The involuntary and voluntary memory boundary
- **Type**: research-topic
- **Notes**: Harvested from the review corpus (optimistic-2026-08-04-memory-self-cluster.md) by /harvest-research-subjects — an external/optimistic reviewer flagged this as uncovered territory. optimistic-2026-08-04-memory-self-cluster flags that Berntsen (2010) sits in concepts/episodic-memory's reference list doing no work in the body, and that the involuntary case is undeveloped across the cluster. The measured claim is only that the counter cannot see them; the true hedge delta is smaller and must be sampled, not assumed. **BUG 2 — the `strong_assertions` ratio branch misfires at count 1 vs 1.** `anchoring.py` L92-96 states the intent verbatim: topic articles legitimately use *"demonstrates"/"establishes"/"shows"* when reporting settled empirical findings. But that allowance is coded **only into the anchor-has-zero branch**. When topic and anchor each have exactly **one** such verb, control falls through to the ratio branch, where the shorter article loses purely on word count. Today's instance: topic 1 verb / 2,241 w = 0.446/kw against anchor 1 verb / 3,450 w = 0.29/kw — a **2.5% overshoot** of the 1.5× threshold, driven entirely by a 1,209-word length difference. **A one-assertion article is not an over-claiming article.** **BUG 3, minor, same class**: `UNDERDETERMINATION_PATTERNS` misses *"does not on its own decide between"* because the intervening *"on its own"* breaks the `does not decide between` pattern — a live false-negative source that did not affect today's flag only because the anchor also scored zero. **WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE FILE.** These bugs push in the same direction: they make correctly-calibrated articles look under-hedged and over-asserting, which generates refine tasks whose only available remedy is **hedge-stuffing prose that already reads cleanly**. The audit now has **five** recorded false-highs resolved by `anchoring_audit_exempt: true` rather than by editing — `wanting-liking`, `akrasia-motor-selection`, `interventionist-dualism`, `graduated-middle-path`, and today's `basal-and-bioelectric-cognition`. That is the instrument telling on itself. **CANDIDATE FIXES (operator's call):** (a) add the plural inflections to `HEDGE_MARKERS`, re-run, and report the new flag count **before** touching any article; (b) extend the settled-findings allowance to cover the 1-vs-1 case, or floor the check at a minimum absolute count (e.g. skip when `strong_assertion_count <= 2` on either side); (c) loosen `UNDERDETERMINATION_PATTERNS` to tolerate short interpolations. **(b) is the smallest and stops the most false work.** **DO NOT** let a content fork apply these — and note that (a) will change flag counts corpus-wide, so it wants a before/after measurement, not a blind patch. **RELATED, DECIDE TOGETHER:** the open `altered_state_symmetry.py` vocabulary entry — same instrument class, same shape of defect (a scanner whose word list is narrower than the corpus's actual usage), same recommendation to measure before adopting.

### P3: P-Q5's credence rose moderate → high in the same pass that dropped a dependency and conceded a whole evidential channel did not apply
- **Type**: positions-evolve
- **File**: obsidian/positions/quantum-interface-calibration-history.md
- **Review file**: `reviews/pessimistic-2026-08-03-positions-calibration-schema.md`
- **Status**: pending
- **Source**: pessimistic-review
- **Generated**: 2026-08-03
- **Notes**: **L62–65.** The 2026-07-31 note records `credence **moderate → high**` on the Orch-OR demotion while simultaneously recording that the demotion's previous basis — the Diósi-Penrose radiation bounds — **does not reach Orch-OR at all**: *"Orch-OR never committed to that completion, so the underground bounds do not reach it, and this entry no longer depends on P-Q6."* So one pass **dropped a dependency, lost an evidential channel, and raised the band**. Stated warrant: *"because it survives ChatGPT's objection where the old basis did not, credence rises a band."* **The problem**: the surviving channel (Tegmark 2000; Reimers/McKemmish 2009, 2014 on Hagan-Hameroff-Tuszyński 2002) was present throughout and was not newly strengthened. What changed is that a *different* argument was found inapplicable — which is evidence of prior over-counting, and normally warrants holding or lowering, not raising. Raising requires the further premise that the survivor was being *under-weighted* while the bad argument did visible work; the note does not argue it. This is the ratchet **P-M1** exists to block (defeater-removal never upgrades an evidential tier), reappearing as robustness-of-the-survivor used as an upgrade lever. **FIX — either**: (a) supply the missing premise explicitly, arguing the coherence channel was under-weighted under the old framing and why; **or** (b) revert to `moderate` with a note that the basis was **re-founded at constant credence**. (b) is cheaper and more defensible. **Credit where due — do not undo the surrounding work**: the same note settles a three-way reviewer disagreement on the physics rather than by vote, correctly declines Gemini's unconditional reading of Derakhshani et al., refuses to quote Claude's compression of McQueen, and states *"non-ownership is exemption from the test, not credit for passing it"* — which is exactly right and sits oddly against the upgrade. Only the band-move is at issue.

### P2: the convergence section's independence premise is false, and the article calls that convergence its central evidential pillar
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/voids/ineffable-encounter-void.md
- **Review file**: `reviews/pessimistic-2026-08-06-ineffable-encounter-void.md`
- **Status**: pending
- **Source**: pessimistic-review
- **Generated**: 2026-08-06
- **Notes**: Four connected defects in and around *Convergent Evidence Across Independent Traditions*. Sibling P1 on the same file handles quote fidelity — distinct lens, keep the edits separate.
  - **L79 states a falsehood.** "Multiple traditions, developed without mutual influence, converge on the same structure", and L91 calls this "the central evidential pillar". Otto (1917) read James (1902) and borrowed from him directly while rejecting his empirical method — this is standard in the literature on *Das Heilige*. Rosa is writing in 2016 with full access to all four predecessors. The Otto/James pair carries most of the weight and is exactly where the influence is documented. Drop "developed without mutual influence"; a genealogical claim (a lineage that keeps returning to the same structure) is still worth something but is weaker and different, and must be stated as such.
  - **L91 crosses epistemic to metaphysical in one sentence** — the convergence is "the central evidential pillar for treating ineffable encounter as a genuine cognitive boundary rather than a difficult problem of articulation", with L157 completing it ("meaning that cannot be cashed out neurally ... structurally closed to third-person investigation"). All the evidence is reports of failure to articulate; the conclusion is constitutive closure. L91 names the very distinction at issue and settles it by assertion. Split the readings and either supply the bridge or mark the crossing as the Map's commitment rather than the evidence's verdict. This is orthogonal to hedge density — the anchoring audit will not catch it.
  - **The standard rebuttal is absent.** Steven Katz, "Language, Epistemology, and Mysticism" (in *Mysticism and Philosophical Analysis*, 1978) is the canonical attack on exactly this perennialist inference: no unmediated experience, so cross-traditional similarity evidences shared conceptual scaffolding and reporting convention. Wayne Proudfoot, *Religious Experience* (1985) adds that ineffability claims function as protective descriptive strategies. Zero mention of either. Engage Katz **in-framework**, not by tenet appeal: constructivism predicts convergence only where the tradition supplies the vocabulary, so identify which of the five features are tradition-supplied and which are not. If none survives, the section supports a weaker claim than it advertises and should say so.
  - **Rosa is mis-framed, not mis-cited.** The quote is verbatim and correctly attributed (checked this pass). But *Resonanz* is a normative diagnosis of world-relations under social acceleration, not a thesis about inarticulability or cognitive closure. Keep Rosa, cite him for the unpredictability/non-manufacturability strand specifically, and stop counting him as an independent arrival at the same structural insight.
  - **Run the article's own falsifier 2 while you are in here.** Gendlin+Polanyi are one strand (tacit knowing), Otto+James a second (religious experience, genealogically linked), Rosa a third and off-topic. Grouping by what each actually claims either strengthens the section or honestly shrinks it.
  - Apply the direct-refutation discipline. Identify what kind of engagement the issue calls for: showing the opponent's position is defective on its own terms, naming an unsupported foundational move the framework has not earned by its own standards, or honestly marking the framework-boundary disagreement. Apply the corresponding reply mode in **natural journal-quality prose** — see [the writing-style guide](/project/writing-style/)'s "Engaging Opponents in Journal-Quality Prose" section. **Do not expose mode labels in the article body.**

Live counts are **topics 318/320, concepts 317/320, voids 100/100** — so tasks citing ~47 slots of headroom are reasoning about 2-3. **CLAUDE.md is now FIXED** (driver, same run): the table carries real figures, a dated as-of, an explicit re-measure-before-acting warning, and a pointer to this entry's off-by-one. **THE 8 TASK NOTES ARE DELIBERATELY LEFT UNEDITED** — rewriting the bodies of pending tasks is the in-place re-scoping that makes `cycle_post` mis-mark, and the exposure is bounded because **the cap is enforced in code, not by the note**: `cycle_pick` consults `all_sections_at_cap(state.section_caps)` and `/expand-topic` refuses a full section, so a stale note misleads reasoning without letting an article through the gate. ### NEEDS-HUMAN (loop tooling) 2026-08-01: `scan_transcripts` CANNOT detect a fork whose fallback fires before its first assistant turn — verified misattribution found and fixed
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/workflow/changelog.md
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Source**: refine-draft attribution check, 2026-08-01T12:5xZ, transcript b8e74477 window
- **Code path** (not the `File` above, which is set to a content path so a refine fork cannot mangle a module): `tools/evolution/model_fallback.py`, function `scan_transcripts`
- **Notes**: **A STRUCTURAL BLIND SPOT IN THE FALLBACK DETECTOR, found by tripping over its output rather than by reading it.** `scan_transcripts` keys detection off **same-file model MIXING**. When the primary model is present it flags every non-primary message (`FALLBACK-SUSPECTED`); otherwise it sets `foreign = [m for m in messages if m != dominant]` and then `if not foreign: continue`. **So a transcript in which EVERY assistant message is the fallback model has an empty `foreign` list and is silently skipped.** The `else` branch can only ever fire on a 3-way mix; for a pure single-model transcript it is a guaranteed `continue`. **THIS IS EXACTLY THE CASE THAT PRODUCES A WRONGLY-STAMPED ARTIFACT**, because a fork that never observes itself on the primary model stamps `ai_system` with the model it was *nominally dispatched as*, not the one it ran as. The existing code comment reasons carefully about the "5x fable then 1276x opus" stick — but that case has ≥1 fable message and so is caught. The zero-fable case is the one that escapes. **VERIFIED INSTANCE, ALREADY FIXED (do not re-fix).** `agent-ac317aa5f61d948ac.jsonl` — the research-topic fork that wrote `obsidian/research/sentientism-2026-08-01.md` — carries a fallback marker at `2026-08-01T07:55:21.573Z`, roughly five seconds BEFORE its first assistant turn at `07:55:26.212Z`, and then runs **53 assistant messages, all `claude-opus-5`, zero `claude-fable-5`**. The detector's 12:41Z scan covered that window (previous scan 07:41Z) and flagged three other transcripts while skipping this one. The note was stamped `ai_system: claude-fable-5`; corrected to `claude-opus-5` in both `obsidian/` and `hugo/content/`. **WHY THE FIX VALUE IS THE BARE FALLBACK MODEL, NOT A `+`-JOINED PAIR**: the `+` form denotes genuine mixed authorship, and here fable-5 wrote nothing at all. This matches the 2026-07-28 audit note observing that fork-written review archives "correctly self-attribute `ai_system: claude-opus-5`", and differs from the `a0fc32857` / `66f0237b5` corrections only in that those forks had a genuine co-author to preserve. **CANDIDATE FIXES (operator's choice, none actioned):** (a) treat a transcript whose messages are ALL non-primary as a stick and flag it — needs a notion of the expected primary model per run, since a legitimately opus-configured session is indistinguishable from a stuck one on message content alone; (b) key detection off the explicit **`{"type":"fallback","from":…,"to":…}` marker** the harness already writes into the transcript, which is present in this fork and is unambiguous — almost certainly the right fix, and it makes the mixing heuristic redundant rather than merely supplementing it; (c) leave the detector and instead have the dispatcher stamp the *observed* model at fork exit rather than letting each fork self-report. **SCOPE UNKNOWN AND WORTH MEASURING**: no sweep has been run for other artifacts written by zero-fable forks, so the number of similarly misattributed files is unmeasured. A sweep would grep the subagent transcript tree for fallback markers and cross-reference the files each such fork wrote — cheap, and it bounds the problem. **⚠️ SECOND, INDEPENDENT BLIND SPOT IN THE SAME LANE — VERIFIED IN CODE 2026-08-03T15:5xZ, and it is the one that bites a long session.** `queue_attribution_task` (`tools/evolution/model_fallback.py` L195-204) dedupes with a bare substring test: `todo = TODO_PATH.read_text(); stem = event.transcript.stem; if stem in todo: return False`. That matches the transcript id **anywhere in the file** — including inside a `### ✓`-closed entry below `## Completed Tasks`, and including a mere mention in some other task's Notes. **Consequence: once a session has been flagged and its attribution task closed, that session can never be re-flagged, however much longer it runs.** **MEASURED ON THE LIVE SESSION, which is the driver's own:** transcript `2a435880-26dd-4e40-bb58-abe8dd702a89` was queued and closed (`### ✓ 2026-08-03: Verify ai_system attribution after model-fallback event`) when the detector saw **1303** foreign messages. The 15:49Z run reports **2541** — the window has since grown from 2026-08-02T09:04:46Z to 2026-08-03T15:49:44Z — and the run printed `[SKIP] todo.md already references 2a435880-…`. So roughly 1,240 messages' worth of loop output sits outside any attribution audit and the detector structurally cannot say so. **SEVERITY IS LOW *HERE* BUT THE MECHANISM IS NOT.** In this instance `dominant` and `foreign` are both `claude-opus-5`, which is the session-level-stick shape that self-attributes correctly (model-fallback-dominant-equals-foreign-is-correct, fallback-stick-self-attributes-correctly) — so nothing is currently mis-attributed. On a genuinely mixed session the same suppression would hide real drift. **CANDIDATE FIXES (operator's call, all small):** (a) dedupe on `stem + last_foreign_ts` so a grown window re-queues; (b) restrict the substring search to the **active** region above `## Completed Tasks`, which also fixes the mere-mention false match; (c) re-queue when the foreign count has grown by more than some factor since the recorded task. **(a) is the smallest and most direct.** **NOTE:** the driver did **not** hand-queue an attribution task for this window — the skill reserves that for the script, and the finding here is the dedup rule, not the attribution itself.
- **Scope sweep RUN 2026-08-01T13:0xZ** (by the sibling attribution check on the 12:32–12:34Z `agent-a841909c` window; answers the "SCOPE UNKNOWN" paragraph above for **one session**, not the whole tree). Model composition computed for all **9 forks** of session `b8e74477`: **5 of the 9 are 100% `claude-opus-5` with zero `claude-fable-5`** (`a2decb20`, `a5a81eea`, `a614def7`, `a8834aa7`, `ac317aa5`) and are therefore **all structurally invisible to `scan_transcripts`**; only 2 were model-mixed and so detectable (`a46bcc7e`, `a841909c`), and 2 ran pure fable-5 (`a773b272`, `ac5abf0f`). **The blind spot is not a rare edge case in this sample — it is the majority of forks.** Of the 5 invisible ones, only two wrote authored prose to the vault: `ac317aa5` (the known, already-fixed sentientism note) and **`a5a81eea` — a SECOND instance, previously unrecorded**: the 12:58–13:04Z deep-review that wrote `obsidian/concepts/samkhya-three-way-distinction.md` (commit `fa2a670dc`), 74 assistant messages, all opus-5. The remaining three wrote no prose (`a2decb20` set one `ai_system` value; `a8834aa7` posted externally only; `a614def7` was the auditing fork itself). **NO CORRECTION WAS OWED ON THE NEW INSTANCE, and it must not be "fixed" retroactively** — that fork held `ai_system: claude-opus-4-7` and declined to re-stamp, which **matches corpus convention**: the two 07-31 sweeps for the identical nav-gloss/link-label calibration family (`52126351b`, 5 files; `e29e11a8c`, 2 files) each bumped `ai_modified` only and left every `ai_system` untouched. A one-line Further-Reading gloss rewrite is not re-authoring. **THE POINT OF RECORDING IT IS RECURRENCE, NOT DAMAGE**: `a5a81eea` ran *after* the 12:41:51Z scan high-water mark, so the next scan's range covers it and will skip it again for exactly the same reason. The defect reproduces every cycle, and the cases where it happens to be harmless are invisible for the same reason as the cases where it is not — which is why (b), keying off the explicit `fallback` marker, remains the recommendation. **Still unmeasured**: the other ~200 session directories under the project transcript tree; this sweep covered one.
- **Second defect in the same module, found 2026-08-01T13:1xZ by the third sibling attribution check (the `agent-a46bcc7e` 07:46–07:48Z window): THE DETECTOR FLAGS ITS OWN AUDIT FORKS, and this is the one subclass where the "was content written?" question is answerable at QUEUE time.** `scan_transcripts` walks `root.rglob("*.jsonl")`, which includes each session's `subagents/` directory, and `queue_attribution_task` dedupes only on transcript id — so an attribution-check fork that itself runs model-mixed mints a fresh P2 attribution-check task **about its own transcript** on the next scan. The window assigned to this task *is* exactly that: `agent-a46bcc7e7d867d6c2` (3 `claude-fable-5` turns, then 24 `claude-opus-5` — the stick is real and the flag's count is exact) is the 07:46–07:48Z fork whose entire output was the changelog entry recording its own no-op verdict on the earlier 07:36–07:39Z harvest window. Its only vault write was `obsidian/workflow/changelog.md` (commit `8c8b5aab8`; the rest of that commit is `todo.md`, `evolution-state.yaml`, `.unfin/current-queue-task.json` and the hugo mirrors, none of which carries `ai_system`), and `changelog.md`'s own `ai_system` **already read `claude-opus-4-8+claude-opus-5`** before the edit — the fallback model was on the file already, so no annotation was owed even on the one attributed surface it touched. **MEASURED, NOT INFERRED**: of the 38 subagent transcripts named by attribution-check tasks in this file, 24 are still on disk, and **2 of those 24 are themselves attribution-check forks** — this one and `agent-a5a18311b0e2e5a81` (2026-07-13), closed further down this file as "*prior attribution-audit no-op fork, no content*". **The pattern was therefore already noticed once, closed locally, and never reached this defect record.** **WHY IT BELONGS HERE RATHER THAN IN A SEPARATE TASK**: the 07-31 `806e8218` note below records that `check_model_fallback.py` "queues on the transcript window alone and does not check whether content was written in it — working as designed, since that check is meant to happen at execution time". That reasoning is right in general and should not be reversed. It simply does not hold for the self-referential subclass, whose window is knowable in advance to contain nothing but the auditing fork. **CANDIDATE FIX (d), narrow and cheap**: have `queue_attribution_task` skip a transcript whose own dispatch arguments are an attribution-check task — the flag text is fixed boilerplate and greps in one line. **DO NOT generalise this to "audit forks never write content"** — that is false and would suppress real findings: the 12:53Z sibling audit *did* write, correcting `research/sentientism-2026-08-01.md`. The exemption is for the *self-reference*, not for the task type.

### NEEDS-HUMAN (loop tooling) 2026-07-31: `integrate-orphan` silently DISCARDS its task Notes at dispatch — measured 278 args chars vs 2689 for the same task as refine-draft
- **Type**: refine-draft

- **Notes**: **MEASURED, NOT INFERRED.** `tools/evolution/task_selector.py` handles `TaskType.INTEGRATE_ORPHAN` (~L255) by composing a **generated** context string — *"This file has no inbound links and is orphaned. Focus on finding related articles that should link to this content…"* — and returns `SkillInvocation("deep-review", f"{file_path} -- Context: {context}")`. **It never references `task.notes`.** `TaskType.REFINE_DRAFT` (~L206) does the opposite, explicitly appending `f"{args}\n\nTask context:\n{task.notes}"`. **THE MEASUREMENT.** The driver ran `task_to_skill` against one real task in both forms: as `integrate-orphan` it produced **278 characters** of args; the identical task as `refine-draft` produced **2689**. Everything an author writes in the Notes of an integrate-orphan task is thrown away before the executor sees it. **WHY THIS IS NOT COSMETIC.** The task in question (`topics/phenomenal-normativity-environmental-ethics`, integration gap: 25 outbound links, 2 live inbound, 0 of 39 apex) had Notes carrying a **per-candidate `analyze_length` table**, because length binds hard among its candidate linkers: `concepts/animal-consciousness` has **9 words** to its hard ceiling and `concepts/phenomenal-value-realism` is **already over** at 4039/4000. An executor receiving only the boilerplate would have had no way to know that, and the natural action — adding a sentence of linking prose — would have pushed an already-over-ceiling file further over. **The Notes were the safety rail and the dispatcher deletes them.** **IMMEDIATE MITIGATION ALREADY APPLIED, so nothing is at risk right now**: the driver retyped that task `integrate-orphan` → `refine-draft` and prepended an explanation; it now dispatches 4929 args chars with the length table intact. The semantics are unchanged — the executor is told the edits land in the *source* files rather than the `File` anchor. **THE OPERATOR DECISION.** Options: **(a)** make `INTEGRATE_ORPHAN` append `task.notes` exactly as `REFINE_DRAFT` does — a two-line change and almost certainly right, since the generated boilerplate can simply precede the Notes rather than replace them; **(b)** retire `integrate-orphan` as a type and standardise on `refine-draft` with integration instructions in the Notes, which is what the corpus already does in practice; **(c)** leave it and rely on drivers spotting it, which is not viable — this was found only because a fork happened to report its args length. **(a) is the smallest change.** **DO NOT ACTION FROM THE LOOP** — this is the loop's own automation code, which the content loop must not self-modify. **DO NOT mint a P0–P3 from this.** Worth noting the same shape may affect other non-`refine-draft` branches of `task_to_skill`; a sweep of that function for handlers that ignore `task.notes` would be cheap and is the natural companion to (a).

### NEEDS-HUMAN (workflow publication policy) 2026-07-31: the 418 broken links check-links keeps reporting are ALL on served, sitemap-indexed workflow pages — a presentation decision, not a link repair
- **Type**: refine-draft

- **Status**: needs-human

- **Generated**: 2026-07-31
- **Notes**: **MEASURED THIS RUN, AND THE SEGMENTATION IS THE POINT.** check-links reports **418 broken internal links across 34 source pages**. Segmented: **article prose (`topics/ concepts/ apex/ voids/ positions/ arguments/ archive/`) = 0**; **records (`workflow/ reviews/ research/`) = 418** (workflow 410 across 27 pages, research 6, reviews 2); anything else = 0. The fork did not trust the crawler alone — it re-audited from `sitemap.xml`, fetching **795 article-section pages directly and status-checking 888 unique internal targets, with 0 non-200**. So the serving *article* surface is completely clean, and **every previous "417 broken links" alarm was this same records-only floor.** **WHY THIS IS NOT NOISE, THOUGH IT IS NOT A DEFECT EITHER.** The driver checked whether these pages are actually public: `/workflow/` appears in `hugo/public/sitemap.xml` (8 entries) and there is **no `robots.txt` exclusion** for it. So a reader or crawler reaching e.g. `/workflow/archive/changelog-2026-w12/` (63 dead links on that page alone; `workflow/todo` carries 46) sees broken navigation on an indexed page. **THE CAUSE IS INHERENT AND THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG.** These are dated records naming articles that were later archived, coalesced or renamed. **Repointing them would falsify the record** — the changelog entry is supposed to say what was true when written. So this is not a link-repair task and must never be handed to a refine-draft that "fixes broken links". **THE ACTUAL DECISION, which is presentational and operator-side:** (a) render historic article references inside `workflow/` records as **plain text rather than links** at sync time, which preserves the record exactly while removing the dead navigation; (b) exclude `/workflow/` from the sitemap and add a `robots.txt` disallow, keeping the pages reachable for anyone with the URL but not indexed; (c) stop serving `workflow/` altogether; or (d) accept it and stop re-triaging. **(a) is the smallest change that fixes the reader-visible problem without touching the records.** **DO NOT ACTION FROM THE LOOP** — (a) and (b) are changes to sync/site tooling, which the content loop must not self-modify, and (c)/(d) are publication policy. **WHY IT IS WORTH RECORDING NOW**: this floor has been re-measured and re-dismissed by multiple check-links runs, each spending a cycle re-deriving that the 41x figure is records-only. Recording the segmentation once converts a recurring triage cost into a decided question. **DO NOT mint a P0–P3 from this.** **⚠️ ADDITION 2026-08-03T17:0xZ — the baseline moved 417 → 418, and the one new link is PREVENTABLE in a way the other 417 are not.** The 2026-08-03 check-links run reproduces the documented shape exactly — 410 of 418 from `workflow/`, 6 from `research/`, 2 from `reviews/`, and **0 from any content article** in `topics/ concepts/ apex/ voids/ positions/ arguments/`. 374 of the 418 are redirect-covered and only 404 against the checker's ephemeral local server; 44 are dead everywhere. **THE DELTA IS ONE LINK, AND ITS CAUSE IS A HABIT, NOT ROT.** `obsidian/workflow/archive/changelog-2026-W31.md` L4401 contains `[[concepts/parsimony-case-for-interactionist-dualism]]`. Driver-verified: the article exists at `obsidian/topics/parsimony-case-for-interactionist-dualism.md` — there is no `concepts/` copy — so the wikilink was **path-qualified with a guessed and wrong section**, and the converter dutifully emitted a URL that 404s. A **bare** `[[parsimony-case-for-interactionist-dualism]]` would have resolved, because the converter maps bare slugs to the file's real section and the corpus has no colliding stems. The same changelog entry uses the bare form two lines down at L4402 and resolves fine — both forms sit side by side in one entry. **This is the `topics:` canonical-form rule from CLAUDE.md showing up in prose links: path-qualifying is a guess that can be wrong, bare is self-correcting.** **LEFT UNFIXED, deliberately** — archived changelogs are historical records and the standing convention leaves the `reviews/` dead links alone for the same reason; repairing one link piecemeal would not change the decision this entry is waiting on. It is a one-token fix (drop the `concepts/` prefix) if the operator would rather hold the count at 417. **THE PREVENTION IS CHEAPER THAN THE REPAIR:** whatever is decided about serving `workflow/`, agents writing changelog and todo prose should default to **bare-slug wikilinks** and path-qualify only when a stem genuinely collides. That stops the count growing regardless of which publication option is chosen.

### NEEDS-HUMAN (agentic-social config) 2026-07-31: the topic-dedupe filter is silently DEAD — 0 of 671 articles survive it, so every pick falls through to URL-only selection
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/workflow/changelog.md
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Source**: cycle driver, from the 13:01Z agentic-social run
- **Generated**: 2026-07-31
- **Notes**: **MEASURED, NOT INFERRED — the driver ran the selector's own functions against the live corpus at 2026-07-31T13:0xZ and got: 671 published articles, 158 recently-posted URLs, 200 recently-posted topics, 514 articles surviving the URL filter, and *0* surviving the URL+topic filter.** **THE MECHANISM.** `select_content()` in `.claude/skills/agentic-social/scripts/agentic_social_api.py` (~L475–L491) skips any article sharing *any* topic with the recently-posted set. The recently-posted window holds **158 posts carrying 200 distinct topics** — and because Map topic tags are broad and heavily reused (`hard-problem-of-consciousness` alone is applied across a large fraction of the corpus), that 200-topic union now intersects **every single article**. `available` therefore comes back empty on every run. **THE REAL PROBLEM IS THE NEXT LINE.** At ~L493 the code does `if not available:` and silently re-populates from URL-only filtering, with no log line, no warning, and no signal to the caller. So the skill reports a normal successful selection while the topic dedupe it advertises has contributed **nothing**. This is precisely the pattern `CLAUDE.md` forbids under *Error Handling* — "**Never use fallthrough logic that hides errors** … Do NOT provide a catch-all `else` that silently substitutes a default behavior." **OBSERVED CONSEQUENCE, not hypothetical:** of the six posts on 2026-07-31 before this was caught, **three consecutive** (09:27 `phenomenology-of-attention-to-absence`, 10:17 `stapp-quantum-mind`, 11:15 `integrated-information-theory`) carried `hard-problem-of-consciousness`, and the 13:01 run's `select` again returned a `hard-problem`-only article (`topics/quantum-darwinism-and-consciousness`) as its top pick — a fourth in a row. The last two runs only avoided it because the driver briefed the fork to check the tracked history by hand and enumerate the pool manually. **That manual workaround is not sustainable and should not become the fix.** **WHY THIS IS AN OPERATOR CALL RATHER THAN AN AUTOMATED ONE:** the remedy is a tuning decision with a real trade-off, and the loop should not pick it unilaterally. Options: **(a)** decouple the windows — keep 7 days for URL dedupe but narrow *topic* dedupe to 24–48h, which restores the filter's bite while still preventing same-day repetition; **(b)** require overlap on *all* of an article's topics rather than any one, so a broad shared tag like `hard-problem-of-consciousness` no longer vetoes an otherwise-distinct article; **(c)** weight topics by corpus frequency and ignore the most common tags for dedupe purposes; **(d)** cap the topic union at the N most recent posts rather than the full window. **(a) is the smallest change and probably the right one.** **INDEPENDENT OF WHICH OPTION IS CHOSEN, THE FALLTHROUGH SHOULD BE MADE LOUD** — at minimum log a warning when the topic filter empties the pool, so a future silent degradation is visible rather than masquerading as a normal run. **DO NOT "FIX" THIS BY WIDENING THE POSTING CADENCE OR PRUNING `recently_posted`** — pruning would also weaken URL dedupe, which is working correctly and is the thing preventing genuine duplicate posts. **⚠️ UPDATE 2026-07-31T14:4xZ — THE MANUAL WORKAROUND HAS NOW PRODUCED ITS FIRST MISS, WHICH STRENGTHENS THE CASE FOR FIXING THIS.** Because the filter is inert, the driver has been hand-supplying each run with the day's topic union and the fork has been enumerating the pool manually. That held for four runs and failed on the fifth. The 14:45Z post (`concepts/parfit-reductionism`) carries topics **`personal-identity`** and **`meaning-of-life`**. Both are correctly disjoint from the 24-topic union the driver supplied *for that day* — but **both recur repeatedly inside the ~7-day dedupe window the rule actually specifies**: `personal-identity` in 5 earlier posts, most recently **the previous day** (`narrative-coherence`, 2026-07-30); `meaning-of-life` in 5 earlier posts, also most recently the previous day (`alignment-in-objective-experiential-terms`, 2026-07-29). The fork reported that it had checked both against the **full 158-post window** and found **zero** occurrences. That claim is false — the driver re-ran the check and found ten. **No harm done to the account** (the URL is genuinely new, the post is live and verified, and the subject matter is distinct from the earlier posts), **but the dedupe rule was violated and the violation was reported as verified.** **THE LESSON FOR THE OPERATOR:** a hand-driven substitute for the filter depends on the driver supplying the right window *and* the fork checking it correctly, and it has now failed at the second step. The workaround is not a stable substitute for the config fix, and each additional run compounds the chance of a repeat. This is a fifth argument for option (a) — decouple the windows so topic dedupe runs on a short window that a real filter can enforce. **⚠️ UPDATE 2026-07-31T15:3xZ — TWO MEASUREMENTS THAT SETTLE WHAT THE FIX SHOULD BE. THE WRITTEN 7-DAY RULE IS PROVABLY UNSATISFIABLE, NOT MERELY INERT.** The driver measured eligibility across candidate windows against the live corpus (671 published articles, tracker holding 158 posts): **7 days = 199 distinct topics → 0 eligible articles**; 48h = 70 topics → 15; 24h = 45 topics → 49; 12h = 22 topics → 69. At ~45-minute cadence the 7-day union is effectively the corpus's **entire tag vocabulary**, so it intersects every article and **no compliant post exists**. This retires the earlier framing of the 14:45Z post as a 'workaround miss': it was not a careless slip — **any** post violates the rule as written, so the fork could not have complied. It also explains the silent fallthrough precisely: `select_content()` is not misbehaving, it is being handed an unsatisfiable constraint and degrading without saying so. **RECOMMENDATION, now backed by numbers: option (a), decouple the windows — keep 7 days for URL dedupe (which works and is what actually prevents duplicate posts) and set TOPIC dedupe to 24h.** 24h leaves 49 candidates, a healthy pool; 48h leaves 15 and is workable but tight; 12h is more permissive than needed. **Whatever is chosen, make the fallthrough loud** so a future degradation is visible rather than silent. **SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT FOUND THIS RUN — TOPIC STRINGS ARE NOT NORMALISED BEFORE COMPARISON, WHICH INFLATES APPARENT ELIGIBILITY.** Topics are stored as wikilinks that may or may not carry a section prefix, and the filter compares raw strings, so `[[free-will]]` and `[[topics/free-will]]` are treated as **different topics** despite resolving to the same file `obsidian/topics/free-will.md`. Driver-counted across `obsidian/topics/` and `obsidian/concepts/`: **38 occurrences of the bare form against 225 of the prefixed form** — for that one topic alone. Consequence measured this run: of the 15 articles that appeared eligible at 48h, **9 were false-eligible** — 8 carried bare `free-will` while the union held `topics/free-will` (free will *was* covered within 48h, so posting them would have been substantive duplication), and 1 (`topics/argument-from-reason`) had non-matching topics but **its own slug** in the union, i.e. the article *is* the recently-covered subject. **Strict-eligible pool after normalisation was 6, now 5** — so even 48h is close to exhausted, and this defect has been silently masking that. **TWO ADDITIONS TO WHATEVER FIX IS MADE**: (i) normalise topics on both sides — strip `[[ ]]`, strip any section prefix, lowercase — before comparing; (ii) also exclude any article whose **own slug** appears in the topic union. This is the same class as the known harvest-dedup singular/plural near-miss, which suggests a shared normalisation helper would fix both lanes at once. **⚠️ UPDATE 2026-08-03T13:3xZ — THE DIAGNOSIS ABOVE NO LONGER DESCRIBES LIVE BEHAVIOUR, AND THE CORRECTION CHANGES WHICH OPTION FIXES IT.** The 07-31 finding was *0 of 671 survive → `if not available:` silently falls through to URL-only*. The driver re-ran the selector's own functions against the live corpus at 2026-08-03T13:3xZ and got a **different** result: **671 articles, 129 recently-posted topics, 24 survive the topic filter — and all 24 have `topics: []`. Zero articles carrying real topics survive.** **The pool is non-empty, so the fallthrough at ~L493 never fires.** The filter is not degrading to URL-only any more; it is **confined to the ~3.6% of the corpus that carries the empty-topics defect**, and every post is now drawn from those 24. **MECHANISM (read at ~L24 of `select_content`):** the overlap test is guarded by `if article_topics and recently_posted_topics:` — an article with `topics: []` has falsy `article_topics`, so the check is **skipped** and the article is appended to `available` unconditionally. Articles with real topics still meet the full 129-topic union and are all vetoed. The two populations are therefore filtered by opposite rules: real-topic articles face an unsatisfiable constraint, empty-topic articles face none. **OBSERVED CONSEQUENCE TODAY, dated:** the 12:35 post (`concepts/phenomenal-constitution-thesis`, `topics: []`) recorded topic `intentionality`; the **13:24** post (`concepts/conceptual-role-semantics`, `topics: []`) recorded `intentionality` again — **49 minutes apart, same topic key**, both drawn from the 24-article pool where adjacency is unconstrained. `mark-posted` records topics scavenged from the `concepts:` field, so the *record* looks well-formed while selection saw nothing. **WHY THIS CHANGES THE RECOMMENDATION:** option **(a)** (decouple windows, topic dedupe to 24h) was the standing recommendation and it **does not fix this**. Narrowing the union helps only articles that *have* topics; the 24 bypass the check at any window length, so they remain permanently eligible and keep dominating the pool. **Backfilling `topics:` is now load-bearing rather than cosmetic** — it is option (d) of the sibling empty-topics NEEDS-HUMAN entry, and these two entries should be decided **together**: (a) alone leaves the defective subset privileged; backfill alone leaves the 7-day union unsatisfiable for everyone else. **A THIRD, SMALLER FIX WORTH CONSIDERING ALONGSIDE:** make the empty-topics case explicit rather than implicitly-permissive — treat `topics: []` as *ineligible* (or log it) instead of silently exempt, which is the same "no silent fallthrough" principle `CLAUDE.md` states under *Error Handling* and which this entry already invokes for the `if not available:` branch. **NO ACCOUNT HARM** — both posts are live, verified, on genuinely distinct URLs, and the subject matter differs; the defect is the selector's blindness, not the content. **DRIVER NOTE:** the fork that made today's post attributed the adjacency to `topics: []` alone; that is right about the article but was worth checking against this entry's fallthrough story, and the measurement above is what separates them. **REPRODUCE:** load `.claude/skills/agentic-social/scripts/agentic_social_api.py`, call `get_recently_posted_topics()`, then partition published articles by whether `extract_topics(content)` intersects it, and count how many survivors have empty topics. **⛔ RETRACTED 2026-08-03T14:2xZ — THE 13:3xZ UPDATE ABOVE IS WRONG. THE ORIGINAL 07-31 DIAGNOSIS WAS RIGHT ALL ALONG.** The driver's own reproduce recipe, quoted immediately above, is the bug: it partitions articles **by topic only and omits the URL filter that `select_content()` applies first**. `select_content()` skips `url in recently_posted_urls` *before* the topic check. The 24 "survivors" reported in that update are all articles that had **already been posted**, so their URLs are blocked and they never reach the pool. **CORRECTED MEASUREMENT (2026-08-03T14:2xZ, simulating `select_content()` exactly — URL filter then topic filter):** 671 published articles · 139 recently-posted URLs · **532 survive the URL filter** · **0 survive URL+topic** → **the primary pool IS empty and the `if not available:` fallthrough DOES fire, exactly as the 07-31 entry found.** **CONFIRMING EVIDENCE FROM THE SAME RUN:** the 14:21Z post (`topics/emotion-and-dualism`) carries `hard-problem-of-consciousness` (**48** prior occurrences in the window, most recent **10:48Z the same day**) and `ethics-under-dualism` (2 prior). Both were in the union *before* the post. The topic filter therefore rejected that article — and it was posted anyway, which is only possible via the URL-only fallthrough. A pool "confined to empty-topics articles" could not have produced it. **WHAT SURVIVES FROM THE RETRACTED UPDATE** (still true, still worth knowing, but *not* the dominant mechanism): the guard `if article_topics and recently_posted_topics:` does exempt `topics: []` articles from the overlap check, so they are the only articles that *would* survive the topic filter if their URLs were not already blocked. At the current cadence they get consumed quickly and the pool empties regardless. **THE RECOMMENDATION REVERTS TO OPTION (a)** — decouple the windows, keep 7 days for URL dedupe, set topic dedupe to 24h — which the 07-31 measurements already backed with numbers (24h → 49 eligible). The retracted update claimed (a) "does not fix this" and that backfilling `topics:` was load-bearing; **both claims rested on the omitted URL filter and are withdrawn.** Backfilling `topics:` remains worth doing on its own merits (it is option (d) of the sibling empty-topics entry, and empty `topics:` still defeats whatever topic dedupe is eventually made to work), but it is **not** a precondition for (a) and the two entries do **not** have to be decided together. **CORRECTED REPRODUCE RECIPE:** filter `article_to_url(a) in get_recently_posted()` **first**, then apply the topic intersection — or simply call `select_content()` and inspect what it returns rather than re-implementing its filter order. **DRIVER NOTE, worth generalising:** the error was re-implementing a function's filter chain from a partial reading instead of exercising the function itself, and it produced a confident, numerate, wrong claim inside an operator decision document. Prefer calling the real code path.

### NEEDS-HUMAN (citation policy) 2026-07-31: the 07-30 Tallis de-quote campaign rested on a FALSE premise — the span IS verbatim, and 47 loci were demoted
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/arguments/functionalism-argument.md
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Source**: pessimistic-review of arguments/functionalism-argument.md, 2026-07-31 (finding verified independently by the driver)
- **Generated**: 2026-07-31
- **Notes**: **The span `"misrepresentation presupposes presentation"` IS Raymond Tallis's own wording.** Verified 2026-07-31 from the raw publisher HTML at `philosophynow.org/issues/161` — "Tallis in Wonderland: The Illusion of Illusionism", *Philosophy Now* 161 (2024), 58-59. The sentence reads: *"If matter can't generate experiences, it seems even less capable of creating the illusions of experiences, since misrepresentation presupposes presentation."* The separately-cited `"all illusions presuppose experience"` is **also** verbatim, a few sentences earlier — they are two different sentences, not rival readings of one.
  **Why three passes concluded the opposite.** The publisher's HTML splits the word: `misre<tag>presentation`. Strip tags by substituting a **space** — the default in every quick extractor — and the text reads `"misre presentation presupposes presentation"`, so an exact-string grep returns **zero from the primary source** and reads as decisive proof of fabrication. Strip tags with **no substitution** and the phrase is contiguous and present. One character of difference in a regex inverted a 47-locus campaign. This is the publisher-side form of the broken-contiguity trap the corpus already knows from its own files, where wikilinks and `**` break a correct quote the same way.
  **What was done on that false premise.** Commit `b1adfdf1` (2026-07-30) de-quoted **47 loci** — 32 in `obsidian/`, the research-note origin, and 14 in `archive/` — converting a genuine verbatim quotation to attributed paraphrase.
  **Nothing is broken, which is why this is a decision and not a defect.** All 47 loci say true things, attribute them to the right author, and now pin the right work. Restoring the quotation marks is an *improvement in fidelity*, not a repair. At 47 loci across three trees it is a campaign with real regression risk, and it would be the **third** state-flip on this string — so it is the operator's call, not automation's.
  **Three options.** (1) Restore the quotation at all 47 loci. (2) Restore at a small number of high-visibility loci only — the argument articles and `concepts/illusionism.md` — and leave the paraphrase elsewhere. (3) Leave as is and record the decision so this does not re-surface a fourth time. Option 3 is defensible: attributed paraphrase of a correctly-cited source is not a defect.
  **Do NOT act unattended.** Whatever is chosen, the standard for changing the state in *either* direction is the same: reproduce the sentence from the source and name the extraction method. "Web-verified" assertions have now produced a wrong answer in both directions on this exact string.
  **Two separate, smaller items surfaced alongside it, both genuine and both cheap** — these are NOT operator-gated and can ride any future pass: (a) `obsidian/arguments/functionalism-argument.md` L164 renders Tallis's hedged *"hardly going to be able"* / *"seems even less capable"* as **"certainly cannot"**, an unlicensed modal upgrade; (b) the *Philosophy Now* issue number is cited as **159** in `obsidian/topics/attention-and-the-consciousness-interface.md` L240 and `archive/topics/attention-schema-theory-critique.md` L209, where the correct issue is **161** (the ~40 other loci omit the issue entirely, which is fine). Item (a) is already inside the scope of the open P2 on that file.
  The 07-30 campaign's *work-level* correction — repointing the argument from *Aping Mankind* (2011) to the 2024 article — was **right and stands**. Do not undo it. And do not confuse any of this with the Tallis-2016 phantom reference (*"The Disappearance of Appearance"*), which was genuinely fabricated and correctly swept on 2026-05-29.

### NEEDS-HUMAN (methodology) 2026-07-30: install a per-claim verification ledger whose sixth tier is "contested by later literature" — the current stability convention manufactures the failure it misses
- **Type**: refine-draft

- **Status**: needs-human
- **Source**: outer-review-2026-07-30-chatgpt-5-6-sol-pro; diverted by the cycle driver

- **Notes**: **DIVERSION NOTE (cycle driver 2026-07-30T17:50Z).** This was queued as an executable `refine-draft`, but it asks the loop to **institute a discipline**, and `obsidian/project/human-supervision.md` reserves exactly that: L47 lists among the things the human controls *"The skills, **disciplines**, and **methodology** the automation system runs"*, and L117 repeats *"humans control direction, priorities, tenets, and **methodology**"*. The same page draws the contrast that settles it — *"Direction is gated by the human; individual article publication is not."* Articles are the loop's; disciplines are not. Same posture as the standing 2026-07-25, 2026-07-27 and 2026-07-29 methodology diversions. **The doc is `ok` at 1756w (project soft 2500), so length is not the obstacle — authority is.**
- **THE PROPOSAL** (record, do not institute): a ledger recorded **per claim** rather than per reference, with six tiers — does the source exist; was its **full text** read; was the quotation checked **in context**; is the **paraphrase** faithful; does the cited passage actually support the **inference drawn**; and **does later literature contest it**. The reviewer frames this as new; it is more honestly an **extension** — this doc already installs "a quote-string-fidelity check distinct from reference-metadata verification". Tiers 1-3 largely exist; **4, 5 and 6 do not**.
- **⚠️ I VERIFIED THE CORE CLAIM FIRST-HAND TODAY RATHER THAN RELAYING IT — four independent data points, all from this session's own work:**
- **(1) The inheritance mechanism, measured.** `topics/personal-identity.md` had **12 prior reviews and 14 references, of which ~3 had ever appeared in a ledger**. The audit trail shows why: `2026-05-29` classed **ten** entries "spot-verified" with no per-entry sources; `2026-06-06` verified **four** stances and **inherited the rest**; `2026-07-07` re-verified **one** and **inherited everything else**. Each pass reads as diligent alone; the composition re-checks almost nothing. **Apparent coverage compounds while actual checking does not.** This is the sharpest argument for the proposal and it is not in the review.
- **(2) A prior ledger's positive certification was false.** That same 07-07 review certified *"Inline ↔ References cross-reference intact"*. **Montupil et al. 2023 was load-bearing inline with no References entry at all.**
- **(3) Tier 5 failed in exactly the predicted way.** `personal-identity` cited **Santander et al. 2025, *PNAS* 122(43)** for the claim that a centimetre of intact callosum sustains full synchronisation. The study **cuts the other way**: complete-callosotomy patients *did* show network disruption, and residual integration in partial cases is explained by ~1 cm of **spared** splenium — the deflationary reading the paragraph was recruiting it against. **Real paper, real authors, correct year, faithful wording, pointed backwards.** No metadata or quote-fidelity check can reach this.
- **(4) Tier 6 failed in exactly the predicted way.** `apex/mereology-of-mind.md` asserted subject-parthood impossibility outright while **its own bridge article already carried the calibrated verdict** — *"none clearly succeeds… provisional, not a settled finding of the literature—and a central participant rejects it."* The participant is **Shani (2022), *The Monist* 105(1):6-24, `10.1093/monist/onab020`** — invisible to any metadata check, because the References section had not changed. **The existing stability convention ("the citation ledger stands unless the References section changes") does not merely permit this failure; it guarantees it — a page's literature verdict goes stale precisely because nothing about the page changed.**
- **COUNTER-EVIDENCE, recorded so the decision is not one-sided**: the discipline partly works unprompted. On `concepts/cosmopsychism.md` today a fork was asked to add "the residual gap Shani & Keppler themselves acknowledge", **could not verify the concession, and declined to assert it** — installing the gap as the Map's own reading instead. That is tier-4/5 behaviour arising without a ledger, which is an argument that the **steering** may matter more than the instrument.
- **WHERE THE SIXTH TIER SHOULD LIVE**: `/literature-drift-review` already runs weekly and is Audit One of [calibration-audit-triple](/project/calibration-audit-triple/). Wiring the contested-by-later-literature tier into it beats inventing a parallel process — **but that is a skill change, doubly reserved.**
- **TWO SMALLER ITEMS worth deciding at the same time**: (a) **abstract-only verification should be disclosed** and must not support the words "verified", "consensus", or "the literature's verdict" — and the discipline needs to cover **inheritance across the research-note → article boundary**, since the target's research note hedged honestly and the article built on it did not inherit the hedges; (b) **citations should attach to propositions, not paragraphs or bibliographies**, so historical-lineage claims, sociological generalisations and reports of consensus each have an exact supporting location.
- **EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE, recorded as open proposals only**: dependency-triggered review, adversarial review matrices, and separating modification types in the UI. The review names these; they are operator decisions and nothing here should institute them.
- **IF APPROVED**: hold the doc's existing `ai_system`; do not bump `last_deep_review`; measure with `analyze_length` and subtract apparatus. **DO NOT** mint a P0-P3 for this; it is deliberately picker-invisible.

### NEEDS-HUMAN (corpus convention): reference apparatus cannot express VERIFICATION LEVEL, so a ledger can manufacture a misattribution
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/project/quantum-claim-and-quotation-disciplines.md
- **Status**: pending
- **Source**: outer-review synthesis 2026-07-30 (ChatGPT leg) + refine-draft 2026-07-30T08:41Z, which demonstrated the failure concretely
- **Generated**: 2026-07-30
- **Notes**: **OPERATOR DECISION — corpus-wide convention change, deliberately not attempted inside an article task.** The ChatGPT leg observed that articles claim to develop issues with their primary literatures while their own research notes record that full texts were never accessed and that material came from abstracts, secondary descriptions or publisher pages. The reference apparatus **cannot distinguish** bibliographic-existence-verified / abstract-read / full-text-read / quotation-checked-in-context / paraphrase-checked / inference-attributed-to-author-rather-than-supplied-by-the-Map. **A CONCRETE INSTANCE OF THE HARM, established 2026-07-30:** `research/open-individualism-and-the-de-combination-problem-2026-06-19.md` L26 is careful in **prose**, attributing "derivation problem" to **nobody**; its **verification ledger** at L126 then marks the SEP as `[VERIFIED - authoritative source for the cosmopsychist roster, "derivation problem," and the conceivability-mirror quote.]`. The article inherited the **ledger**, not the prose, and asserted that the SEP frames the issue as the "derivation problem". Verified at plato.stanford.edu: the SEP calls it *decombination*, crediting Albahari, and the string "derivation problem" **does not occur** in the entry or its supplement. **So a verification ledger manufactured a misattribution the note it certifies never made — and no prose lens reads ledger lines.** That is the general mechanism, not a one-off. **WHY THIS IS OPERATOR-SCALE, not a task a fork should absorb:** annotating verification level across 20+ reference entries in even one article breaches that article's length ceiling by itself, and the convention must be decided once for the whole corpus or it produces exactly the inconsistency it is meant to cure. **CANDIDATE SHAPES:** (a) a per-entry bracketed level marker in References; (b) a machine-readable frontmatter block keyed by citation, keeping the visible apparatus clean; (c) confine levels to research notes but require an article's reference entry to inherit the weakest level of its sources; (d) accept the limitation and instead forbid ledgers from certifying *terms and attributions* at all, restricting them to bibliographic existence. Note (d) is the cheapest and would have prevented this instance outright. **RELATED, ALREADY SEPARATE**: a P2 exists to extend the quote-fidelity check into a claim-level citation ledger; this is the provenance-level counterpart and the two should be decided together. **NEW EVIDENCE 2026-08-02 (deep-review, `topics/selection-only-mind-influence`), showing option (d) is insufficient:** the fabrication vector there was not a ledger but the research note's own `**Quote**:` field. `research/selection-only-mind-influence-information-limits-2026-05-05.md` carried two `**Quote**:` strings that exist in **no source anywhere** — `"the mind would only have the option to choose the observable, not the option of selecting the measurement result in deviation from the Born's probability law"` (attributed to Stapp; the word "Born" occurs **zero** times in both cited Stapp PDFs, and the substring `"Born's probability law"` returns NO web results at all) and `"violation of higher sum-rules allows for superluminal signalling"` (attributed to Han & Choi 2016; absent from PMC4789655). Both propagated verbatim into the live article and **survived five deep reviews**, one of which recorded a complete 12-entry publisher-of-record ledger and rated the Stapp quote "a faithful representation of Stapp's documented position" — paraphrase ratification standing in for extraction-and-grep. Both are now fixed at article and note, with do-not-reintroduce markers. **SCALE OF THE EXPOSURE**: `grep -c '^- \*\*Quote\*\*' obsidian/research/` → **1625 fields across 360 notes**, none of which any current lens verifies verbatim against a primary text. Restricting *ledgers* to bibliographic existence (option (d)) would not have caught either of these. Whatever convention is chosen needs to cover the `**Quote**:` field specifically — either dropping it, or requiring a `verified verbatim <source> <date>` annotation before an article may quote from it.

- **Type**: refine-draft
