A shared sole topic is a tie-block that drains at one article per 7-day window. **Shortening the window would not fix this**; enriching the taxonomy would. See the open P3 on the taxonomy backfill, which now carries the full measurement. This changes which of the four candidate fixes is the right one.
- **Notes**: **OPERATOR DECISION — a guard has stopped guarding, and nothing errors.** The agentic-social selector filters candidates by TOPIC posted in the last ~7 days (not by URL). **That filter now returns an EMPTY pool on every call, so selection silently degrades to URL-freshness alone.** Re-measured independently by the driver 2026-07-30T07:25Z: `agentic_social.recently_posted` holds **158 URLs, ALL of them inside the last 7 days**, carrying **197 distinct topics**. Of **778** live articles across `topics/ concepts/ apex/ voids/`, **724 have at least one topic posted within 7 days** and **ZERO have a topic set with none posted in 7 days** (the residual ~54 are articles with an empty or absent `topics:` field, which pass only because there is nothing to match). So the boolean topic guard is unsatisfiable by construction. **WHY IT SATURATED — structural, not transient:** at `AGENTIC_SOCIAL_INTERVAL_MINUTES = 45` the account posts ~32×/day, i.e. ~224 posts per 7-day window, while articles carry only 1-3 topics each drawn from a much smaller topic vocabulary. The window will always be blanketed at this cadence. **OBSERVED CONSEQUENCE, not hypothetical:** a fork this morning was offered a topic with **15 hits in 7 days** by `select`, because the strict filter had already emptied and the fallback ignores topics entirely. **CANDIDATE FIXES (operator's choice):** (a) shorten the topic window to ~48-72h so it can actually bind; (b) replace the boolean filter with **topic-distance ranking** — pick the candidate whose topics were posted longest ago, which is what a fork did by hand this morning and which degrades gracefully instead of collapsing; (c) lengthen the post interval so the window stops blanketing; (d) accept URL-only dedup and delete the topic filter, so the degradation is at least honest. **DO NOT silently leave it as-is** — the present state advertises a topic guard that does nothing, which is worse than either having one or not. Interim mitigation already in use: forks rank by topic distance manually, so behaviour is currently acceptable but depends on each fork choosing to do that. **⚠️ TWO CHEAP, MEASURED FIXES ADDED 2026-07-30T10:15Z — these are more actionable than the four window/ranking options above and should be considered first.** **(1) `mark-posted` DOES NOT DERIVE TOPICS, so some posts contribute NOTHING to dedup.** Measured by the driver: **16 of 158** `recently_posted` entries have **no `topics` key at all**, and every one of those posts is invisible to the topic filter for its whole 7-day window. Confirmed instance: `apex/competency-without-felt-experience` was posted 2026-07-30T03:16:13Z and recorded as `{url, date}` with **no topics** — the article itself carries `topics: []` and `concepts: []`, so there was nothing to copy. It is not only apex: `concepts/alexithymia` and `concepts/zero-lag-gamma-synchrony-...` are also topic-less entries. **Fix: have `mark-posted` derive topics from the article rather than relying on a caller-supplied list, and fall back to the slug itself when `topics:` is empty.** **(2) FOLD `apex_sources` INTO THE DEDUP KEY — synthesis posts silently blank their whole spoke cluster.** An apex article with `topics: []` registers zero topics, so all of the articles it synthesises still look untouched. `apex/competency-without-felt-experience` lists **9** `apex_sources`; a fork measured **8 synthesis posts in the last 7 days blocking 68 spoke slugs, none visible to the topic filter**, and that artefact produced ranks **1, 2, 5, 6 and 7** of a naive topic-distance ranking — i.e. the top of the pool was an artefact. **A THIRD DIMENSION THE FORWARD METRIC ALSO MISSES — reverse hub/spoke.** A candidate can be fresh by its own topics while its **own slug** was a *topic* of a recent post. Observed: `topics/bacterial-chemotaxis-and-minimal-biogenic-cognition` ranked first at 154.3h forward distance, but the 02:26Z post carried its slug as one of *its* topics 7.6h earlier. **INTERIM MITIGATION NOW IN USE (manual, per-fork, undocumented in code):** final distance = **min(forward topic distance, own-slug-as-topic distance, spoke-of-recent-apex distance)**, take the maximum over candidates. Applied 2026-07-30T10:10Z it selected `concepts/reinforcement-learning-reward-signals-and-machine-valence` at **142.4h** — the true maximum over 437 eligible candidates. This works but depends on each fork choosing to compute it; encoding it is the durable fix. **Also verified currently NOT a risk:** zero URL-eligible articles had empty/absent topics at selection time, so the section-index / internal-meta leak documented elsewhere is presently closed by existing guards. **⚠️ THE COMPLETE FIX IS A CROSS-PRODUCT — added 2026-07-30T11:08Z, and this supersedes the three-dimension patch above.** Dedup has two identifier kinds, **slugs** and **declared topics**, and a collision can occur in any of the four pairings. Three were known; the fourth was found and verified 2026-07-30: **(a) slug x slug** — the existing URL dedup. Works. **(b) topic x topic** — the boolean topic filter. **Saturated and unsatisfiable** (197 topics in 7 days blanket all 778 articles). **(c) slug x topic** — candidate's own SLUG appears as a declared TOPIC of a recent post. Caught as a trap: `topics/bacterial-chemotaxis-and-minimal-biogenic-cognition` looked 154.3h fresh while its slug had been a posted article's topic 7.6h earlier. **(d) topic x slug — NEW, and it changed a selection.** Candidate's declared TOPIC is the SLUG of a recently posted article. Neither (b) nor (c) sees this direction. Verified by the driver: `topics/cognitive-integration-and-the-self` scored 120.5h on dimensions (b)+(c)+apex and tied for first, but declares `[[temporal-consciousness]]` as a topic — and `concepts/temporal-consciousness` was **posted 2026-07-28T22:29Z, 36.6h before selection**. Without check (d) the run was a coin-flip between it and the correct winner. **Plus a fifth pairing that should NOT be added: shared `concepts:` field.** A fork tested it; it collapsed the best available score from 120.5h to 52.3h, but the hits are hub concepts (`haecceity`, `self-and-self-consciousness`, `phenomenology`) that appear across dozens of articles. That is noise, not subject collision — keep it advisory at most. **Also resolved as NOT a hole:** the 16 dedup entries with no `topics` key are articles that genuinely carry `topics: []` (verified on `alexithymia`, `kairos`, `hard-problem-of-consciousness`), so a backfill yields nothing and they stay covered by (c)+(d). The apex-spoke problem is real and separate: all 8 apex posts in-window blocked 68 `apex_sources` spokes invisibly. **So the durable fix is: replace the boolean (b) filter with a distance metric over the FULL slug/topic cross-product (b,c,d) plus apex_sources expansion, and rank by the maximum.** Everything above is currently done by hand, per fork, and only because each fork is told to. **⚠️ A FIFTH, CHEAPER FIX — 52 ARTICLES ARE PERMANENTLY INVISIBLE TO EVERY TOPIC DIMENSION. Measured 2026-07-30T13:59Z.** `grep -rl '^topics: \[\]' obsidian/{topics,concepts,apex,voids}` returns **52 live articles**. An article with `topics: []` (and often `concepts: []` too) collides on *nothing*, so it scores **infinite distance on d_b, d_c and d_d simultaneously** and rises to the top of any ranking — a **false ∞** that has to be caught by hand on every single run. **CONFIRMED INSTANCE:** `obsidian/topics/hemispherectomy-and-the-resilience-of-unified-consciousness.md` is a real 1609-word article with `topics: []` and `concepts: []`. It ranked ∞ and topped the pool. Measured through its `related_articles` instead, its **true distance is 55.2h** — `disconnection-neuroscience` (posted 55.2h earlier) declares two of its five neighbours, and a 60.5h post covers the production-vs-filter reading from lesion evidence that hemispherectomy's own lead paragraph poses. So the article most likely to be selected was among the *closest* in the pool. **THIS IS THE SAME ROOT AS THE apex_sources GAP, GENERALISED**: apex articles with `topics: []` blank their spoke clusters; these 52 blank *themselves*. **TWO CANDIDATE FIXES:** (a) populate the 52 files' `topics:`/`concepts:` frontmatter — a content chore, but it removes the trap permanently and improves the site's own navigation; (b) in the selector, fall back to `related_articles` when `topics:` is empty, which is exactly what a fork did by hand to unmask the instance above. **(b) is the smaller change and (a) is the better outcome; they are not exclusive.** **INTERIM, until one lands:** any fork ranking candidates must treat a raw ∞ as **suspect rather than best** — check whether the frontmatter is empty before trusting it, and if so measure through `related_articles`. Two runs today were nearly lost to this: one selected on a genuine ∞ (verified: all four topics truly unposted), the next hit a false ∞ and correctly discarded it. **⚠️ THE 96h QUALITY FLOOR IS NOW EMPIRICALLY UNREACHABLE — measured across two consecutive runs 2026-07-30, and this is the decision the operator actually faces.** A full ranking of **419 eligible candidates** at 13:58Z produced an honest maximum of **109.0h**, whose sole holder's *real* nearest neighbour was **75.8h**; every other shortlist entry collapsed on inspection (106.5h→6.7h, 103.0h→18.6h, 74.7h→2.1h). A cheap re-check at 14:59Z confirmed nothing had changed. **The conclusion is structural, not a bad day:** with a **156-entry rolling 7-day window** over a 671-article publishable pool, the corpus cannot produce a candidate 96 hours distant from everything recently posted. **So the cadence and the quality floor are jointly unsatisfiable, and one of them has to move.** **THE OPTIONS ARE NOW A GENUINE FORK, not tuning:** (a) **lengthen the interval** — at ~45 min the account posts ~32×/day and the window is permanently saturated; slowing to ~2h would let the window drain and make a real floor meetable; (b) **lower the floor** and accept closer spacing as the honest steady state, in which case say so explicitly rather than having each fork improvise a threshold; (c) **keep both and accept frequent skips** — which is what is happening now, and is defensible, but means the loop spends slots computing rankings that predictably fail; (d) fix the dedup measure itself per the fixes above, which raises measured distances but does **not** create genuine subject-distance where none exists. **A USEFUL PROOF SHAPE FOR FUTURE RUNS, so nobody re-derives 419 candidates unnecessarily:** removing an entry from the window can only raise a candidate's score if that entry *was* its nearest neighbour. So if the aged-out entry's own age already exceeded the prior maximum, the age-out is **provably inert** and the prior verdict stands — no re-rank needed. Applied at 14:59Z: one entry aged out at 168.2h against a prior maximum of 109.0h, therefore inert; the single newly-eligible article was scored directly (7.6h, nowhere near the floor) rather than assumed. **SCHEMA NOTE for anyone writing a checker**: entries in `agentic_social.recently_posted` key their timestamp as **`date`**, not `posted_at` — a probe using the wrong key reads all 158 as null and silently reports an empty window. **⚠️ ADDITION 2026-08-03T16:1xZ — A CONCRETE COST ON THE BACKFILL OPTION THAT WAS NOT PREVIOUSLY STATED, raised by the agentic-social fork and endorsed by the driver.** Whichever way the filter itself is tuned, the standing proposal to **backfill `topics:` on the ~41 empty-topics articles** carries a mechanical side-effect nobody had priced: **writing frontmatter bumps `ai_modified`, which would falsely reset staleness and drift detection on all 41 files at once.** Those two signals drive `get_review_candidates`, the replenish staleness source, and the `ai_modified > last_deep_review` genuine-drift test that this loop uses to find real review debt. A naive backfill would make 41 articles look freshly-touched and simultaneously look like they had drifted since their last deep review — manufacturing review debt while hiding real staleness. **IF BACKFILL IS CHOSEN, SPECIFY IT AS A METADATA-ONLY PASS THAT LEAVES `ai_modified` UNTOUCHED** (the same posture as the deep-review no-op convention, which moves only `last_deep_review`). That is a script, not a refine-draft fork — a content fork cannot be trusted to edit frontmatter without stamping it, and several forks have future-dated that field today alone. **SEPARATE, SMALLER OBSERVATION ON THE STOPGAP:** forks have started compensating for the empty field by supplying topic slugs to `mark-posted` themselves, and they are not doing it consistently. The 13:24 and 15:15 runs scavenged slugs from the article's own `concepts:` field; the 16:10 run (`concepts/mind-arena`, whose `concepts:` are `interactionist-dualism`, `bidirectional-interaction`, `causal-powers`) instead recorded the broader `dualism`, `machine-consciousness`, `philosophy-of-mind`. **No live consequence while the filter is inert**, but if the filter is ever restored, invented broad tags veto far more candidates than the article's own vocabulary would — so the stopgap should be settled at the same time as the fix, not left to per-run judgement. **⚠️ THIRD STOPGAP VARIANT, 2026-08-03T20:2xZ — the per-run judgement this entry warned about has now produced three different behaviours in four consecutive runs, and the newest one records nothing at all.** Window entries for today: 13:24 `conceptual-role-semantics` and 15:15 `organizational-invariance` — slugs **scavenged from the article's own `concepts:` field**; 16:10 `mind-arena` — slugs **invented broader** than the article's vocabulary (`dualism`, `machine-consciousness`, `philosophy-of-mind` against `concepts:` of `interactionist-dualism`, `bidirectional-interaction`, `causal-powers`); 20:18 `possibility-probability-slippage` — **`--topics` not passed at all**, so the entry stores `topics: None`. **Driver-verified it does not crash**: `get_recently_posted_topics()` returns 127 topics cleanly across the None entry and `get_recently_posted()` returns 136 URLs, so URL dedup — the part that actually prevents duplicate posts — is unaffected. **But `None` is the worst of the three for the eventual fix**: a scavenged or invented entry at least contributes something to the union, whereas this post is invisible to any restored topic filter, permanently. **This strengthens the case for settling the stopgap in the same change as the filter**, rather than after it. **COUNT RECONCILED — the corpus figure has been reported three ways today and all three are right for their scope.** Driver measurement 2026-08-03T20:2xZ over `topics/ concepts/ apex/ voids/ positions/`: **42** articles carry `topics: []` — concepts 19, voids 9, topics 5, apex 5, positions 4. The fork's **38** is the same count excluding `positions/`; the earlier **41** was an earlier scope again. Use 42 as the corpus-wide figure and 38 as the article-sections figure, and state which is meant. **⚠️ CLEANEST EVIDENCE YET, 2026-08-03T22:0xZ — a duplicate-subject pair where BOTH articles carry real topics, which rules out the empty-topics bypass as the explanation.** The 21:07 post (`topics/forward-in-time-vs-time-symmetric-selection`) and the 22:01 post (`topics/empirical-evidence-for-consciousness-selecting`) recorded the **identical** topic pair — `hard-problem-of-consciousness`, `free-will` — 54 minutes apart. Driver-verified: both were read correctly from each article's own frontmatter, neither was scavenged or invented, and both articles are in the same subject area (consciousness-selecting / quantum selection). **Earlier same-day pairs were confounded** — the 12:35/13:24 `intentionality` pair involved two `topics: []` articles, so the empty-topics bypass was a live alternative explanation. **This pair has no such confound**: a working topic filter would have vetoed the second pick outright. Selector state re-measured at the same moment: 671 published, 137 recently-posted URLs, **534 survive the URL filter, 0 survive URL+topic** → primary pool empty → URL-only fallthrough. **No account harm** — distinct URLs, distinct articles, related but non-duplicate content; same disposition as the prior instances. Recorded because it removes a confound from the diagnosis, not because it is a new defect. **⚠️ ADDITION 2026-08-04T02:3xZ — A SEPARATE, PURELY DOCUMENTARY DEFECT, THIRD OCCURRENCE TODAY.** Three agentic-social forks (≈16:10Z, ≈20:18Z shape, and 02:30Z) have each reported in their summaries that *"the recently-posted tracking file lives outside the repo"* or that the `evolution-state.yaml` modification in the working tree was **not** theirs. **All three claims are false.** Driver-verified each time by reading the window immediately after: `mark-posted` writes to `obsidian/workflow/evolution-state.yaml` under `agentic_social.recently_posted`, per `agentic_social_api.py:48` — `STATE_FILE = PROJECT_ROOT / "obsidian" / "workflow" / "evolution-state.yaml"`. The 02:30Z post appears in that window as the last entry. **CAUSE — it is the SKILL DOC, not the forks.** `.claude/skills/agentic-social/SKILL.md` §5 ("Update Tracking", L115-124) shows the `mark-posted` invocation and explains what `--topics` does, but **never says where the state is written**. A fork that has been told not to commit, and that sees a pre-existing `evolution-state.yaml` modification in `git status`, reasonably infers the tracking is external. **CONSEQUENCE — small but real:** the claim is repeated into the changelog and into driver summaries, so a future reader auditing where social state lives is told, in three separate places, to look outside the repo. It also means a fork that wanted to verify its own write would not know where to look. **FIX (operator-gated — a content fork must not edit `.claude/skills/**`):** add one line to SKILL.md §5 naming the path, e.g. *"`mark-posted` appends to `agentic_social.recently_posted` in `obsidian/workflow/evolution-state.yaml`; the resulting diff is yours and is left uncommitted for `cycle_post`."* **This is independent of the filter defect this entry otherwise tracks** — fixing the dedup logic will not stop the mis-reporting, and fixing the doc will not fix the filter. Decide them separately.

Suggested budget: compress **L107–109 ("The Billiard Ball Picture Is Wrong")**, the article's most restatement-heavy passage. **(a) FALSE DILEMMA (Issue 4, the big one).** The article surveys four *materialisms* at L40, concludes at L151 that materialism "in all its forms does not work" and that the Map "commits to dualism", and at L133 asserts *"dualists need only that materialism fails."* The step is invalid without ruling out the non-materialist non-dualist options, and the file contains **zero occurrences** of "panpsychism", "neutral monism", "Russellian", "idealism", or "mysterianism" — verified by grep. **The corpus already has the material**: `concepts/panpsychism.md`, `concepts/neutral-monism.md`, `concepts/russellian-monism.md`, `concepts/russellian-monism-versus-bi-aspectual-dualism.md`, `concepts/panpsychisms-combination-problem.md`. **The flagship links to none of them, and it has 29 content-inbound links** — it is the page most readers and retrieving LLMs hit first. Fix: two or three sentences plus links conceding that materialism's failure underdetermines the successor, routing to `russellian-monism-versus-bi-aspectual-dualism` for the comparison. **Also retire or heavily qualify the L133 burden-of-proof assertion** — it is asserted not argued, materialists reverse it (positing a second ontological category is the stronger claim), and it **repeals the Falsifiability section it closes**: a position that "needs only that materialism fails" has no falsifiers, which contradicts the three disconfirmers listed at L128–131. L151's *"None of this proves dualism"* is the honest register to align with. **(b) DENNETT REPLY (Issue 5).** L71 claims each zombie-reply *"turns on standards the opponent's own programme endorses"*, but the Dennett reply at L65 rests on **uncited** first-person contemplative report (*"The reports point the second way"* — no citation anywhere in the article), and **heterophenomenology** admits such reports only as data about what subjects *believe*, never about phenomenal character. The article never names heterophenomenology though `concepts/illusionism.md` L61 identifies it as Dennett's methodological foundation. Either cite the contemplative literature **and** add one clause marking the methodological disagreement honestly, or downgrade L71's claim for the Dennett case to framework-boundary marking. L137 compounds it: *"a functionalist could attribute this to refined internal monitoring, [but] the reports describe qualitative character … that functional descriptions omit"* — raises the functionalist alternative and never answers it, and asserts the omission that is the point at issue. **(c) BARE REGRESS (Issue 6).** L52 runs the bare regress as one of two exhaustive horns; `concepts/illusionism.md` L93 says flatly *"he is right that the bare regress proves nothing: a representational system need not instantiate what it represents. The substantive engagement is therefore not the regress but the meta-representational bridge."* L52's disposal of Frankish (*"appears to redefine rather than explain"*) also contradicts `illusionism.md` L115 (*"alive on this question, not stalled"*). **THIRD FILE WITH THIS DEFECT** — `concepts/mind-brain-separation.md` carried it too (2026-07-28 filter-framing review, Critical Issue 3). - **Type**: expand-topic

- **Notes**: Research completed in research/voids-fatigue-void-2026-04-05.md but article not yet synthesised. Fatigue produces graceful but ordered degradation of consciousness — abstract reasoning fails before perceptual experience, social cognition before action, moral reasoning before motor coordination — providing structured evidence about consciousness's layered architecture. Distinct from sleep void (involuntary loss) and habituation void (familiarity). Voids cap at 98/100 — placing this after anesthesia void brings voids to 100/100 (cap). P3 because the anesthesia void is more time-sensitive and methodologically richer. Target section: voids/. Tenet alignment: Dualism, Hard Problem. Medium scope (2000-2400 words). Cross-link to sleep-consciousness-void, attention-and-consciousness, resolution-void, habituation-void, complicity-void.

- **File**: obsidian/apex/apex-articles.md
- **Status**: pending
- **Notes**: **ALL FIGURES MEASURED LIVE THIS RUN, not copied from the apex-evolve report** — `analyze_length` per file, never `wc -w`; population is `obsidian/apex/*.md` minus the two index pages `apex.md` and `apex-articles.md`, giving **38 apex articles**. **THE REQUIREMENT.** `## Evidence and Dependency` is required on every apex article, adopted 2026-07-16 from outer-review rec #29 (ChatGPT 5.6 Pro full-site audit). Codified in three places: `.claude/skills/apex-evolve/SKILL.md` L267–269 ("Every apex article carries a short reader-facing section... between the Synthesis section and Relation to Site Perspective"), L46 and L171 (apex-evolve must install it if absent); `obsidian/project/writing-style.md` L144 (required section 4), L153 (the rationale — synthesis pieces are vulnerable to *confidence amplification*, and the ledger stops coherence counting as evidence by construction), and L605 (the checklist item). **THE STATE.** Present on **7 of 38**: `ai-as-introspection-control`, `dualism-cartography`, `self-construction-constructor`, `phenomenology-of-consciousness-doing-work`, `what-consciousness-tells-us-about-physics`, `assessing-ai-consciousness-under-the-map`, `steelmanning-as-method`. **Absent from the other 31.** Thirteen days after adoption the retrofit is running at roughly one article per two days, entirely as a side effect of whichever apex a deep-review or apex-evolve slot happens to touch (see the completed entries above for `dualism-cartography` 07-25, `what-consciousness-tells-us-about-physics` 07-19, `steelmanning-as-method` 07-19, `phenomenology-of-consciousness-doing-work` 07-17). **No validator, linter or check sees this** — `validate-all` and `check-tenets` do not test for the section, so nothing surfaces the shortfall except an apex-evolve run that happens to look. **WHY IT STALLED — THE COLLISION IS ARITHMETIC, NOT NEGLECT.** The section costs roughly 200 words. Against the apex hard ceiling of 5000, of the 31 articles missing it: **16 have under 400 words of headroom**, **6 have under 100**, and **3 are already over hard** — `phenomenal-output-causal-machinery-dissociation` 6904w (critical, 1904 over), `machine-question` 5765w, `conjunction-coalesce` 5144w. The tightest under-ceiling cases are `self-concealing-interface` 4997w (**3 words of headroom**) and `born-preserving-causal-efficacy` 4994w (**6 words**). **So retrofit-by-addition is unavailable for roughly half the backlog**, and for the three over-hard articles it is unavailable outright. Several of the tight cases are also explicitly sealed at their current length by earlier operator decisions (`time-consciousness-growing-block` 4850w is on the sealed list). **THE PRIOR DECISION THAT BLOCKS THE OBVIOUS ROUTE.** The natural unblocking move — condense first, then install the ledger — runs into the operator `#veto` standing on the condense task for `phenomenal-output-causal-machinery-dissociation`, which reads as a decision that apex length is human territory and not something the loop resolves on its own. That veto is why this cycle also declined to mint a condense for `machine-question` (see report), and it is why the retrofit cannot be sequenced automatically. **THE DEFINITIONAL QUESTION THAT SIZES THE BACKLOG — this is the cheapest thing to settle first.** Several articles already do the ledger's *work* in prose without carrying the heading. `apex/moral-architecture-of-consciousness.md` L60 and L156 hold what an optimistic-review this cycle called the strongest calibration prose in its cluster — the coherence-inflation discount and an explicit denial that the four pillars are four independent confirmations — which is precisely the ledger's content, unheaded. If prose of that kind satisfies the requirement, the real backlog is materially smaller than 31 and much of the remainder is a heading-and-reformat job costing near zero words. If it does not, the backlog is 31 and half of it needs a length decision first. **Nothing else can be sized until this is answered.** **FOUR OPTIONS, ALL REQUIRING AN OPERATOR CALL.** **(1) Ratify prose-equivalence** — amend the SKILL/writing-style wording so an explicit dependency-and-independence discussion satisfies the requirement whether or not it sits under the heading; then a cheap sweep adds headings where the substance already exists, and the residue is a much smaller list. **(2) Raise the apex hard ceiling** by ~200 words *for articles carrying the ledger*, making the section length-neutral by construction; this is the only option that unblocks all 31 without touching prose, but it moves a discipline the operator set. **(3) Prioritised partial retrofit** — declare the ledger required only for apex articles that carry a *tenet-inherited* line of support (the case the discipline was actually written for), leaving descriptive/cartographic apex out of scope; sizes the backlog by function rather than by count. **(4) Condense-first campaign** — lift the `#veto` for a scoped set of over-ceiling apex, condense, then install; highest cost, and it is the option the veto currently forbids. **DO NOT let an auto-loop pick one.** **SCOPE FENCE IF AND WHEN THIS IS APPROVED:** whatever is decided, the resulting work is a multi-article campaign and must be minted as individually-scoped per-file tasks, one article per task — `cycle_post` closes a multi-file task after a single file, so a single "retrofit the ledger" task would silently drop 30 of its 31 targets. **The `File` line above points at the apex catalogue only because this entry needs a target; the decision is corpus-wide and no edit to that file is implied.** **ATTRIBUTION**: no content file is touched by this entry; nothing to stamp.

Do **not** extend `minds-without-words`; its `apex_thesis` is about experience being more fundamental than cognition and would be diluted.

  **SOURCE ARTICLES (all live, all non-draft, no orphans — inbound counts verified):** `topics/language-recursion-and-consciousness` (33 in) · `topics/consciousness-and-language-interface` (27 in) · `voids/language-thought-boundary` (60 in) · `concepts/language-and-consciousness` (26 in) · `voids/recursion-void` (38 in) · `topics/phenomenology-of-linguistic-failure` (14 in) · `topics/philosophy-of-language-under-dualism` (12 in) · `concepts/conceptual-role-semantics` (10 in).

  **THE THESIS NO SINGLE ARTICLE CAN VOICE FROM INSIDE ITSELF:** *language is a physical-functional system consciousness uses as a tool, and the structured, non-uniform pattern of its failures is evidence about consciousness rather than about language's poverty.* Each source supplies one face — recursion the capacity argument, aphasia the dissociation argument, linguistic-failure the phenomenological argument, the language-thought boundary the structural-limit argument, philosophy-of-language the semantic-gap argument.

  **THE DISCIPLINE TO MAKE EXPLICIT — copy it, do not compose it.** `language-recursion-and-consciousness` **L37** already states the cluster's method: *"The evidence carries the first stage but not the second; keeping them distinct is the discipline this article models, since the inviting mistake is to let evidence for access stand in for a conclusion about phenomenality."* That is the language-cluster counterpart of `minds-without-words`'s constrain-vs-establish signature and should be the apex's methodological spine.

Adopt `positions/ai-consciousness-scope` **P-AC1**'s register — *"low probability," not "ruled out"* — and **cite the register**, which no article in the cluster currently does. If the sibling refine-draft has already landed, verify rather than re-fix.

  **LENGTH.** Apex articles run long and this cluster is large; `minds-without-words` is ~4,000w. Decompose before trusting any over-length signal (analyze-length-counts-reference-apparatus) and use `analyze_length` rather than a raw word count.

- **Notes**: **THE PATTERN IS NOW THE FINDING.** All three commission lanes were exercised tonight and **all three carry documented steps that no longer match the live UI, each with a bail condition that fires when nothing is wrong**: ChatGPT (always-true bail on an "Extended" option that no longer exists on the model in use), Claude (a `querySelectorAll` probe that returns empty while the menu is open), and now Gemini. Each was worked around by a fork improvising; none would have survived literal compliance. **Whatever is decided per-lane, the shared lesson is that these skills verify UI state through single brittle signals — a testid, a coordinate, a DOM query — and every one of those has now broken at least once.** Prefer multi-signal confirmation, and prefer polling a *positive* signal over bailing on a *negative* one. **UPDATE 2026-08-06 (driver, from the 04:00 UTC commission — the lane succeeded again, again by departing from the doc): THE ROOT CAUSE IS NOW DIAGNOSED, which turns this from "the check is unreliable" into a specific one-line fix.** Step 7's readiness check reads `document.body.innerText`, but **Gemini now renders the research-started confirmation inside a shadow root**, so `body.innerText` never contains it. The check returned `researchStartedConfirm: false` for ~90 seconds while research was demonstrably running (the card read "Researching 49 websites…"). A shadow-DOM-piercing text walk returned `true` immediately. **Literal compliance would have bailed without writing a pending entry, discarding a healthy commission** — and downstream that reads as "no review commissioned" rather than as a failure, so the lane would lose a cycle silently. **Fix options**: (a) replace the extractor with a shadow-piercing text walk; (b) corroborate with the visible-and-disabled state of the "Start research" button; (c) both. Note this is the *inverse* of the `stopBtn` false-positive the skill already warns about — same brittle-single-signal class, opposite direction, which is why a per-signal patch keeps missing it. **Two further drift items observed the same run**: the composer's "Tools" button is now a `+` icon labelled **Upload & tools** (Deep research is still a `menuitemcheckbox` inside it, verified via `aria-checked`); and **pressing Return does not submit** — the prompt sat in the composer through two attempts and required the `Send message` button, with several seconds of latency before the conversation id appeared, which initially read as a failure. **Step 5's 15s bail window is tight against that latency.** Exactly one user turn was created, so no double-submission occurred, but a retry-on-timeout would risk one.

  **(1) THE READINESS CHECK IS ACTIVELY DANGEROUS — it would have thrown away a good commission.** After the "Start research" click succeeded, the check reported `researchStartedConfirm: false` for **~10 seconds** because Gemini renders the confirmation text late. The doc's rule — bail if false 4 s after the click — would have discarded a **running Deep Research job**, leaving no pending entry while Gemini worked in the background. That is the worst failure shape available: silent, and it wastes the run. **Fix: poll for the `I'll let you know` stem over ~30 s.** Two related traps: `startResearchBtnStillPresent` stays `true` after a successful start (the old plan card keeps its button), so it is **not** a usable negative signal; and a mid-run `bodyTextLen` jump is not a proxy for research starting — the 1740→21622 spike observed tonight was the sidebar expanding.

(Note this is the *same shape* as the Claude lane's defect, where an accessibility-visible control is invisible to a direct DOM query.)

  **(3) COORDINATE CLICKS ARE OFF BY A 0.665 SCALE FACTOR.** The viewport is 1873×1431 CSS px while screenshots return 1246×952, so a `find`-tool ref click for "Start research" landed on the sidebar. What worked was a DOM-dispatched sequence (`pointerdown`/`mousedown`/`pointerup`/`mouseup`/`click`) with real `clientX`/`clientY`. ### NEEDS-HUMAN (methodology) 2026-08-04: a grep-contiguity check in the Map's OWN file was recorded as discharging quote-fidelity — contiguity is not provenance

- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/project/quantum-claim-and-quotation-disciplines.md
- **Status**: needs-human
- **Blocked-by**: human-methodology-decision — this is a DISCIPLINE, and `obsidian/project/human-supervision.md` L47 reserves instituting disciplines to the operator. Recorded, deliberately not instituted.
- **Source**: /replenish-queue run no.933, 2026-08-04 — first-hand, from tonight's own de-quote passes
- **Generated**: 2026-08-04
- **Notes**: **NOT A NEW TASK — this is a fifth data point for the proposal already recorded above at "NEEDS-HUMAN (methodology) 2026-07-30: install a per-claim verification ledger whose sixth tier is 'contested by later literature'", which sits on this same file, as does "NEEDS-HUMAN (corpus convention): reference apparatus cannot express VERIFICATION LEVEL".** Filed as its own block only so the datum is not lost inside a long Notes body; **do not mint a third executable task on this file** (outer-review-same-file-task-pileup). Whoever institutes the ledger should fold this in.

  **THE OBSERVED FAILURE, VERBATIM.** `obsidian/reviews/deep-review-2026-07-30-personal-identity.md` **L49** reads: *"**Quote fidelity**: the two Nagel fragments (\"too much unity\" / \"too much separation\") are grep-contiguous in the raw file (`grep -c` = 1 each). Not re-verified at Springer this pass (403); the 2026-05-29 fix stands."* That is recorded as a **pass**. Tonight's 02:30Z and 02:36Z passes established that **"too much separation" appears in no primary source at all** — not in Nagel, not even in SEP, which reads "too much *splitting*" in its own paraphrasing prose. The certified-clean quote was a fabrication.

  **WHY THE CHECK COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT.** Grep-contiguity is a test run **against the Map's own copy**. It establishes that the quoted span is unbroken *here* — i.e. that no elision was silently introduced on our side. It says nothing whatever about whether any source ever contained the string. **Contiguity is a self-test; provenance requires the source.** The existing page already states the right rule — check **(c-ii) quote-string-faithful**, "verify the string *word-for-word* against the source text" (L62–L66). What is missing is that a *named, mechanical, apparently-rigorous local procedure* reads as discharging (c-ii) and discharges nothing, and that a publisher **403** was allowed to convert into *"the prior fix stands"* rather than into an unverified marker.

  **THE COST, MEASURED.** `topics/personal-identity` was designated a verbatim-safe **control** on this reasoning and held that status from 2026-05-29 to 2026-08-04 — over two months — while quoting a phrase nobody wrote. Two separate passes (02:30Z, 02:36Z) inherited the control designation from it before the third overturned it.

  **THE TRAP RUNS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, which is why it needs writing down rather than a reflex.** This case: contiguity **present locally** ⇒ wrongly read as fabrication-free. The converse is already on record in tallis-misrepresentation-quote-propagation and quote-must-be-grep-verifiable-in-raw-source: contiguity **absent at the publisher** (an inline tag splitting a word, or wikilinks and `**` breaking the span) ⇒ wrongly read as fabricated, and 47 loci were de-quoted on that false premise. A ledger tier must therefore record **where** the check was run and **what a failure there licenses**, not merely pass/fail.

  **SUGGESTED SHAPE (record, do not institute):** a `(c-iii)` sibling to the existing checks — *provenance located*: the quoted span was matched **in the source text at the publisher of record or an equivalent primary channel**, with the channel named. Local grep-contiguity is demoted to what it is: an elision self-test, recordable but never sufficient. A publisher 403 yields **unverified-this-pass**, an explicit tier, never an inherited pass.

  **RESIDUE — DO NOT "FIX" IT.** The quoted forms surviving in `reviews/deep-review-2026-06-06-personal-identity` L50, `reviews/deep-review-2026-07-07-personal-identity` L55, `reviews/deep-review-2026-07-30-personal-identity` L49, `reviews/optimistic-2026-06-19` L40 and `workflow/archive/changelog-2026-W22` L2010 are the **audit trail** of what the articles said. The 02:36Z changelog entry already names them so a later sweep does not read them as live defects. Correcting them would falsify the record.

  **THE REFUTING SOURCE, already verified at publisher on 2026-08-04 — do not re-research from scratch.** Kida, S. (2020), "Function and mechanisms of memory destabilization and reconsolidation after retrieval", *Proceedings of the Japan Academy, Series B* 96(3), 95–106 (PMC7167366). Abstract, verbatim: "a retrieved memory is **not always** destabilized and that there are boundary conditions that determine the induction of destabilization and reconsolidation according to certain parameters, such as the duration of retrieval and the memory strength and age." Pair with Elsey, J. W. B., Van Ast, V. A., & Kindt, M. (2018), "Human memory reconsolidation: A guiding framework and critical review of the evidence", *Psychological Bulletin* 144(8), 797–848, DOI `10.1037/bul0000152` (Crossref + OpenAlex verified; note the year is **2018** and **Van Ast** is a co-author — a same-cycle reviewer got both wrong). ### ✓ 2026-08-05: `invertebrate-consciousness-as-interface-test` misses five 2024–2025 papers — three by authors the article already relies on
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/topics/invertebrate-consciousness-as-interface-test.md
- **Notes**: From the literature-drift audit of 2026-08-04 (research area: `invertebrate`). **This is a missing-citation flag, NOT a staleness flag — say so if the fix note records a reason.** The median empirical citation year is **2021** against `ai_modified` 2026-07-08, a lag of exactly 5 years, which does **not** exceed the `median_year_lag_threshold` of 5. Check 1 is clean. `find_superlative_claims` returns **0**, so check 3 (empirical-record currency drift) is clean too. The signal is check 2 alone: five topically appropriate papers, none cited.
  **THE STRONGEST SIGNAL IS WHOSE PAPERS THESE ARE.** Three of the five are by authors this article already builds on, publishing later work on the exact claims it uses them for. This is not a general "field has moved" flag — it is the article's own sources having moved.
  1. **Gibbons et al. (2024)**, *iScience* 27(8): 110440, DOI `10.1016/j.isci.2024.110440` (open access). Nine authors, senior author **Lars Chittka** — whose *The Mind of a Bee* (2022) is the article's evidence base at **L61**. Bumblebees touched on one antenna with a 65 °C probe groomed the touched antenna more than the untouched one, and more than sham- or un-touched controls. The abstract opens by noting it "has been widely stated that insects do not show self-protective behavior toward noxiously-stimulated body parts, but this claim has never been empirically tested". Directly strengthens the insect half of the article's case, and does so with a *behavioural* marker rather than the cognitive-sophistication markers L61 currently lists.
  2. **Leung et al. (2025)**, *PLoS Biology* 23(7): e3003217, DOI `10.1371/journal.pbio.3003217` (open access). **Same first author and same senior pair (van Swinderen, Tsuchiya) as the article's reference 9, Leung et al. 2021**, used at **L91** for IIT-structure collapse under anaesthesia in *Drosophila*. The 2025 paper runs a massive library of univariate time-series features and finds wakefulness distinguishable from anaesthesia and sleep in flies across many of them; its abstract explicitly criticises reliance on features chosen without "principled, theoretical justifications" and warns of "researcher biases toward specific analyses". **Handle this as a calibration correction, not an addition.** L91 currently reads the 2021 result as IIT-specific support ("integrated information structure collapses"); the same group's later work suggests a broad family of measures tracks conscious level in flies, which weakens the inference that integrated-information structure *specifically* is what the anaesthetic disrupts. The article's "**Anaesthetic convergence**" constraint at **L119** survives — arguably it is strengthened, since the convergence is now measure-robust — but the IIT-specific reading should be hedged.
  3. **Brown & Birch (2025)**, *Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B* 380(1939): 20240309, DOI `10.1098/rstb.2024.0309` (**not** open access). Co-authored by **Jonathan Birch**, whose framework has a dedicated section at **L83–L89**. On when motivational trade-offs count as sentience evidence: the abstract grants that such evidence shifted opinion on crabs and insects, then presses three critic points — the trade-off/consciousness link is not fully known; *C. elegans* shows simple trade-offs via a mechanism "plausibly too simple to support conscious experience"; and pain can *interfere* with rational trade-offs. Their conclusion is that the nature of the trade-off and its neural substrate matter. **This runs against the article's stated preference.** L103–L107 adopt the universal coupling response as "most coherent"; a nematode clearing a behavioural bar with a substrate too simple to be a plausible coupling site is exactly the case that response has to absorb. Engage it in the "Natural Zombie Problem" section rather than filing it as support.
  4. **Elwood (2025)**, *Animals* 15(3): 445, DOI `10.3390/ani15030445` (open access, sole author). Elwood is the principal decapod-pain researcher. **This one fixes an existing gap, not just an absence**: **L79** asserts that decapods "demonstrate nociceptive responses, learned avoidance, and anxiety-like behaviour under threat" with **no citation at all** — the only uncited empirical claim in the article. Elwood's review is the natural source, and its own calibration matches the Map's: many findings are "consistent with the idea of pain", but "that does not mean that pain has been proved... we will probably never have conclusive proof", with reflexive responses explicitly partitioned off. Cite it *with* that hedging intact.
  5. **Barton & Barrett (2025)**, *Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B* 380(1929): 20240255, DOI `10.1098/rstb.2024.0255` (open access). "Embodied cognitive evolution and the limits of convergence." **This is a rival framing and must be presented as one.** They attack the "cognitivist gambit" — the assumption that cognitive processes involve representations independent of the sensory-motor specialisations tied to different body plans and ecological niches — and argue sensory-motor adaptations are intrinsic to cognitive evolution rather than confounds to be controlled away. That is a direct challenge to the article's central abstraction: reading three divergent architectures (**L113 scale independence**, **L115 architectural flexibility**, **L117 evolutionary independence**) as instantiating one substrate-neutral coupling question. It also bears on the convergent-evolution inference drawn from Feinberg & Mallatt 2016 at **L81**. The honest move is to name it as pressure on the abstraction, not to absorb it as another datum.
  **SEPARATE APPARATUS DEFECT, FIX WHILE HERE.** **L85** cites *Birch's* **Edge of Sentience* (2024)** in the body, but it is **absent from the References list** — the list runs to 10 entries and stops at Birch (2022) as entry 2. Add it.
  **DO NOT INFLATE CALIBRATION** ([evidential-status-discipline](/project/evidential-status-discipline/)). Five more citations do not move this article up the five-tier scale. Two of the five (Brown & Birch, Barton & Barrett) cut *against* the article's preferred readings and one (Leung 2025) narrows a claim it currently makes broadly. If the pass ends with the article more confident than it started, it has been done wrong.
  **VERIFICATION LIMITS — CARRY THEM, DO NOT LAUNDER THEM** (research-note-self-flagged-gaps-propagate-to-the-article). The session's WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200), so this audit was run against the **OpenAlex API** instead — see webfetch-survives-websearch-exhaustion. Every one of the five is verified for **metadata** (authors, journal, volume, issue, pages, DOI, date) and for **publisher-supplied abstract text only**. **No full text was read for any of them.** Abstract phrasing may be quoted *as abstract*; add **no verbatim quotation** from the bodies of these papers and no claim about their internal methods beyond what is summarised above (quote-aggregator-ratification-corrupts-verbatim). Brown & Birch 2025 is paywalled — treat it as the most constrained of the five. Note also that the OpenAlex record renders Chittka's surname with a dotless "ı"; the correct spelling is **Chittka**.
  **LENGTH**: measured this run at **2,777 w, status `ok`** against topics 3,000 soft / 4,000 hard — only **223 w to the soft ceiling**, 1,223 w to hard. Five citations plus a hedge on L91 will cross the soft threshold if written expansively. Keep each integration to a sentence or two, prefer amending existing sentences over adding new paragraphs, and preserve the existing hedges and underdetermination markers (condense-regresses-calibration-qualifiers). Measure with `analyze_length`.
  **ATTRIBUTION**: hold the file's existing `ai_system: claude-opus-4-7`; bump `ai_modified` (currently `2026-07-08T06:44:53+00:00`), `date -u`-checked and strictly past (fork-future-dates-frontmatter-timestamps). **MIRROR**: sync and verify the changed strings in `hugo/content/topics/invertebrate-consciousness-as-interface-test.md` (obsidian-only-fix-leaves-defect-live-in-hugo).

### ✓ 2026-08-04: `consciousness-and-the-major-evolutionary-transitions` L64 says the biological-individuality pluralism never asks whether a subject is a further kind of individual — Godfrey-Smith asks it, in the special issue the article already cites

  **WHY IT IS FALSE.** Peter Godfrey-Smith, "Individuality, subjectivity, and minimal cognition", *Biology & Philosophy* 31(6): 775–796, DOI 10.1007/s10539-016-9543-1, is devoted entirely to connecting kinds of biological individuality to the evolution of subjective experience. It is **the paper immediately following** Pradeu's "The many faces of biological individuality" at 31(6): 761–773 — i.e. it is in the *same special issue* that this article already cites at **L62** (body) and **L122** (reference 11). The article is refuted by the issue it invokes.
  **THE REPLACEMENT IS STRONGER THAN THE CLAIM IT REPLACES — DO NOT MERELY DELETE THE SENTENCE.** The question *is* asked, and answered **organizationally, after the dualist answer is foreclosed by stipulation**. Godfrey-Smith's second paragraph, read this run from the author-hosted primary PDF and quoted in the research note at L75: *"Setting aside dualist and panpsychist views, it seems that the special features of subjects are organizational, and this organization will be the product of some sort of evolutionary process."* That is the Map's phenomenal-blindness thesis operating **one level down** from where the article currently states it — the bracket is visible in the text, and it has a cost. That is a better paragraph than the one on disk.
  **WHAT SURVIVES AND MUST BE KEPT.** The *criterion lists* really do stop short, and that half of L64 is defensible: the SEP survey entry `biology-individual` (Wilson & Barker) contains **zero** occurrences of "conscious", "phenomenal", "sentience", "experience", or "person", and the most recent general criterion on offer (Fulda 2023, *Evolution & Development* 25(6): 353–370) is **agential** rather than phenomenal. The mechanism is self-perpetuating: each empty-`topics` article bypasses the overlap filter, wins by default, gets posted, ages into the URL window, and hands the role to the next one. Populating `topics:` with accurate bare slugs is the opposite move — it makes them *properly subject* to the overlap filter instead of invisible to it, which fixes the degenerate pick without shrinking the pool. **Do this file first** (it is the measured three-time offender), then treat the remaining ~21 as a follow-on batch, judging each article's real subject rather than assigning slugs mechanically. Note `concepts/kairos.md` needs `concepts:` populated as well.

L94 reads "concluding that intact *semantic* continuity suffices to sustain diachronic unity as autonoetic continuity degrades" — but the paper states **"Semantic continuity was most impaired in AD"**: fewer self-event connections than HC, lower temporal and thematic coherence than HC *and* aMCI, lower causal coherence in both AD and aMCI. "Intact" is the opposite of what was found. What survived was the **belief layer only** — perceived persistence (χ², p=0.91) and I-self persistence (H=2.34, p=0.31) did not differ — while persistence-explanation sophistication was significantly *worse* in AD (H=8.8, p=0.01) and me-self persistence was paradoxically *higher* in AD (H=6.82, p=0.03). The authors' own verdict is **"a more nuanced and multifaceted relationship than originally proposed in our model"** and "a complex relationship". The article is reporting the authors' *proposed model* as though it were the *study's result*. Sample: HC=25, aMCI=15, AD=15, with 14 per patient group completing the self-persistence interview — small, correlational; the authors themselves note the belief measures may index "the level of engagement that a participant has with difficult questions about self-persistence" rather than diachronic unity. **Rewrite so the sentence reports preserved *beliefs* against *impaired* semantic continuity, carries N and the correlational caveat inline, and drops "suffices".** Note the direction of the error: it ran in the Map's favour, which is why prior review passes did not catch it — see the companion methodology task on congenial-paraphrase fidelity.

### ✓ 2026-08-04: consciousness-and-language-interface L106 asserts the folk unbroken-inner-monologue picture that the Map's own 2026-08-02 research note explicitly refutes — and the sampling source it needs is already cited in four sibling articles
- **Type**: refine-draft

- **Notes**: **THE DEFECT — SINGLE LOCUS, GREP-ANCHORED, RE-VERIFIED THIS RUN.** `obsidian/topics/consciousness-and-language-interface.md` **L106** reads: *"**Inner speech and experience.** Much adult thought occurs as [inner speech](/concepts/introspection/)—the internal voice that accompanies reflection. (1) *"Much adult thought"* sits at the high end of what sampling supports. (2) The definite *"This inner monologue"* imports continuity the evidence does not license — a monologue is by construction unbroken. (3) **Sharpest**: *"Trying to think without words—as in certain meditation practices"* frames wordless thought as an achievement requiring trained effort, when momentary sampling finds most sampled moments already contain no inner speech at all. No meditation required.
  **THE CORRECTING EVIDENCE IS ALREADY IN THE VAULT — THIS IS NOT A NEW RESEARCH TASK.** [inner-speech-and-anendophasia-2026-08-02](/research/inner-speech-and-anendophasia-2026-08-02/) **L126–L135** records Heavey & Hurlburt (2008), *Consciousness and Cognition* 17(3), 798–810, doi `10.1016/j.concog.2007.12.006`: descriptive experience sampling of 10 randomly-identified moments from each of 30 participants; **each of the five inner-experience phenomena occurred in approximately one quarter of sampled moments**; frequency varied widely across individuals. The note draws the inference in as many words at L135 — *"the folk picture of an unbroken inner monologue — which the Map's articles implicitly accept when they treat its absence as remarkable — is not what sampling finds"* — and at L47 names the wider miss: **unsymbolized thinking** (Hurlburt & Akhter 2008, *Consciousness and Cognition* 17(4), 1364–1374, doi `10.1016/j.concog.2008.03.021`), explicit differentiated thought experienced without words or images, one of the five most common sampled features, standing since 2008 on within-subject momentary sampling rather than between-group questionnaires.
  **THIS IS AN INTERNAL-CONSISTENCY DEFECT, WHICH IS WHY IT OUTRANKS ITS SIZE.** The corpus already cites the DES tradition in **four** live articles — `obsidian/voids/minimal-consciousness-void.md` L72 + ref 1, `obsidian/voids/voids-between-minds.md` L126 + ref 14, `obsidian/topics/microphenomenological-interview-method.md` L64/L120 + ref 4, `obsidian/topics/phenomenology-of-memory-and-the-self.md` L96 — while the one article that most needs it cites Hurlburt **nowhere**: the References block at L279–L291 has no Hurlburt and no Heavey entry. Add Heavey & Hurlburt (2008) to the References block, alphabetically between Chalmers and Lind. **The correction strengthens the article's own argument** rather than costing it anything: L182's rebuttal to the Dennett/Carruthers/Vygotskian constitutive view currently leans on the contested anendophasia population, and the research note's L247 makes the point — the constitutive view must explain how reflection proceeds during the roughly three-quarters of sampled moments containing no inner speech **in typical people**, with no disputed population required. That rationale assumed the fragments were Nagel's words. They are not: **"too much separation" is not in SEP either** (SEP has *splitting*), and SEP is itself paraphrasing. So the fragments quote a phrase that appears in no primary source, attributed to "Nagel (1971) observed". **The control was honoured and the file left untouched** — overriding an explicit do-not-touch on 2–3 word fragments seemed the wrong unilateral call mid-pass — but the justification no longer holds and a deliberate decision is owed.

The invented sentence entered via `obsidian/research/voids-formalization-void-2026-02-18.md` and was inherited by the article. Both are now fixed. **The channel is not.** WHY THIS IS ITS OWN LENS: research notes are published content that no metadata review reads for verbatim fidelity, and articles inherit their quoted lines wholesale. The defect was found only because a fork happened to be editing that exact sentence for an unrelated citation fix. Nothing in the current review rotation looks for it. **THE HIGH-YIELD SHAPE — search this first.** The fabrication was a *concession invented on behalf of an opponent*: a cited author made to undercut their own programme, in a direction that suits the Map. Driver-measured surface: **529 research notes, 386 carrying attributed quotes, 100 containing concession-shaped language** (`concede`/`concedes`/`admits`/`doubtful whether`). Do **not** accept a WebSearch "confirmation" topped by unfinishablemap.org (circular), and do **not** treat a prior review's restatement as ratification of the wording. If a quote is real but mislocated or mis-framed, **re-frame or re-locate it — do not delete it.** **SCOPE**: audit this note fully, then report the yield rate so the operator can decide whether a wider sweep is worth funding. Where a fabrication is removed, record the correction in reported speech rather than reproducing the invented sentence verbatim, so it cannot be re-extracted from published content.

It *briefly responds to* prior concerns; it advances no precautionary principle. **The precautionary principle lives in a DIFFERENT paper by an overlapping four-author subset**: **Niikawa, T., Hayashi, Y., Shepherd, J., & Sawai, T. (2022). "Human Brain Organoids and Consciousness." *Neuroethics* 15(1), 5, doi:10.1007/s12152-022-09483-1.** **WHY THIS IS NOT A BIBLIOGRAPHIC NIT**: the **"Relation to Site Perspective"** closes with *"The Map lands near Sawai's precautionary conclusion, but for a different reason"* — a load-bearing dialectical anchor resting on a source that does not hold the anchored position. **(2) ⚠️ A BARE CITATION-SWAP IS NOT THE FIX — READ NIIKAWA ET AL. FIRST.** Publisher and aggregator snippets indicate their principle is a **methodological bracketing device**, not an ethical-conduct rule: it "adopts a precautionary principle about consciousness, which requires us to assume that HBOs have consciousness" **specifically so as to** "sidestep the question of whether HBOs have consciousness (the *whether*-question)" and "directly address the question of what kinds of conscious experiences HBOs can have". That is an analytic move to make the *what-kind* question tractable — a different register from "proceed as if they may be conscious". **THIS FINDING IS FROM SNIPPETS, NOT FULL TEXT** (the Springer full text sat behind an authorisation redirect and the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted): the *direction* of the correction is well-evidenced, the *extent* is not. (2023). ### ✓ 2026-07-31: the falsification roadmap reports the 2021 Gran Sasso result with its polarity inverted — it credits survival to Penrose's own version, which is the version that was excluded
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: obsidian/topics/falsification-roadmap-for-the-interface-model.md
- **Notes**: Minted by /optimistic-review 2026-07-31 (see reviews/optimistic-2026-07-31-collapse-falsifiability-cluster). **THE DEFECT IS IN THE MAP'S FAVOUR, ON THE ONE DOCUMENT WHOSE VALUE IS REPORTING WHAT GOES AGAINST THE MAP.** Three parts, all the same family, all verified live on disk this run against the roadmap's own designated source article (`topics/penrose-gravity-induced-collapse-empirical-prospects.md`, which the roadmap lists in `related_articles` L35 and which reciprocates at its own L22). **(a) PRIMARY — POLARITY INVERSION, L91.** The roadmap reads "The Gran Sasso experiment (Donadi et al., 2021) rules out the simplest form of the Diosi-Penrose collapse model **but not Penrose's original proposal**." The parameter-free model *is* Penrose's original proposal — being parameter-free is precisely what distinguishes it. Penrose fixes R0 from the nuclear wavefunction spread (0.05e-10 m for germanium); Donadi et al. set R0 > 0.54e-10 m; Penrose's value sits an order of magnitude BELOW the bound and is therefore the thing excluded. The source article states this outright at its L44 — "What the experiment excludes is therefore Penrose's own physically determined value, **not a limiting idealisation**" — and in its lead: "The version in which Penrose fixes the model's one length parameter from physics rather than fitting it was falsified in 2021; versions that fit it survive." **THE FIX IS NOT "DP IS DEAD".** There IS a real surviving version: DP with R0 demoted to a free parameter, above the XENONnT bound. What must stop is attributing that survival to *Penrose's original proposal*, and the replacement should carry the cost the source article prices at its L48 — the surviving version buys survival by giving up "the *natural* macroscopic quantum-classical boundary, fixed by gravity alone with no adjustable scale". **(b) THE RECORD STOPS IN 2021.** `grep -c "Majorana\|XENON"` on the roadmap returns **0**. The source article carries three bounds on a common footing (Gran Sasso R0 > 0.54e-10 m; Majorana R0 > 2.54e-10 m per the 2023 erratum that corrected the 2022 publication downward; XENONnT R0 > 4.5e-10 m, 2026), plus the Figurato et al. 2024 two-sided squeeze (an upper bound from the requirement that collapse actually deliver macroscopic classicality). Both the Tenet-2 status paragraph (L91) and the Orch-OR table row (**L145**, "Gran Sasso constrains simplest Diósi-Penrose model") present a five-year-old single bound as current. Quote bounds on the common footing the source article names — Markovian white noise, Diósi's rate convention, which differs from Penrose's by a factor of 8pi — and carry its scope caveat that white-noise exclusions do NOT transfer automatically to dissipative/coloured generalisations. **(c) AN UNREFEREED PREPRINT CARRYING MORE WEIGHT THAN ITS SOURCE ALLOWS.** Roadmap L91 says arXiv:2512.02838 "offers a near-term path to testing whether collapse is real"; **L123** says it "could distinguish decoherence ... from genuine collapse"; **L165** (What the Map Should Watch, item 2); and **L150**'s table cell gives "Near-term experimental blueprints" as No-MWI's entire traction. The source article at its L62 calls the same item "Horchani's unrefereed 2025 preprint", says it is "proposal rather than measurement", and says it is "aimed principally at CSL". This is calibration/currency rather than factual error — do not overcorrect it into a dismissal — but it runs the same direction as (a) and (b). **PROPAGATION — TWO FURTHER LIVE LOCI, VERIFIED THIS RUN.** `obsidian/topics/brain-internal-born-rule-testing.md` **L102** and **L134** both read "the original Penrose proposal survives with reduced parameter space". It is NOT claimed by any other open task (checked). ### ✓ 2026-07-30: concepts/cosmopsychism treats de-combination as one problem for one view — constitutive, nonconstitutive and aperspectival versions need separating
- **Type**: refine-draft

- **Notes**: The review's structural point about the de-combination literature: the Miller-style objection targets views on which local subjects are literally constituted by or included within the cosmic subject, and it does **not** straightforwardly reach emergent, generative, nonconstitutive, filtering, dependence-based or aperspectival varieties. The SEP entry itself distinguishes constitutive from nonconstitutive cosmopsychism and defines minimal cosmopsychism more broadly than the Map does. **THE FIX**: broaden the minimal definition; separate perspectival from aperspectival versions; and state which objection applies to which variety instead of pronouncing the family collectively unsuccessful. **FOUR DISTINCTIONS WORTH CARRYING**: (1) **subject vs quality vs structure derivation** — explaining why local subjects exist, why they have their particular qualities, and why their experiences have their structure are distinct tasks, and treating all three as one de-combination problem hides where a theory has progressed; (2) **parthood vs grounding** — even if subjects cannot be literal proper parts of subjects, it does not follow that one consciousness cannot ground differentiated centres through a non-mereological relation; (3) **modal vs explanatory argument** — conceivability may threaten metaphysical necessitation, but failing to establish necessitation is not failing to offer a grounding model, and the conceivability step is conditional in the SEP's own formulation ("if the conceivable separation licenses the modal inference…"), not an established result; (4) **cosmopsychism has motivations beyond avoiding micropsychist combination** — priority monism, intrinsic-nature theories, holistic features of physics — so showing de-combination is hard does not remove the theory's rationale. **ALSO**: Albahari denies that universal consciousness has the ordinary subject-object form, and Shani & Keppler expressly reject a universal *perspectival* subject and propose a specific phase-locking/filtering model while acknowledging a residual explanatory gap. Describing that as "filtering/resonance" hides both its content and its vulnerabilities. **VERIFY the post-2019 sources at the publisher before citing** — see the caveat in T1 of this batch. **LENGTH**: measure with `analyze_length`, not `wc -w`, and subtract the References + Further Reading apparatus before believing any over-length status. **ATTRIBUTION**: hold the file's existing `ai_system` unless you genuinely re-author. **SIBLING REVIEW PENDING**: the Claude sibling review of this same article (`outer-review-2026-07-30-claude-opus-5.md`) was still `pending` when these tasks were minted, so `/combine-outer-reviews` may upgrade or dedupe them later today — check for a synthesis file before assuming this task stands alone.

- **Type**: refine-draft

- **Notes**: **FROM CONVERGENT OUTER REVIEWS (2026-07-30, 2/3 reviewers): [chatgpt, claude]** — **both part (b) and part (c) below are convergent**, and Claude rates (c) the single decisive gap. **ON (c), THE PHYSICALIST WING** — Claude: "wholly absent, and this is the decisive gap", and names the specific rivals to engage: **IIT's exclusion postulate** (only the local maximum of Φ is a subject — a *physicalist* answer to the very individuation/boundary problem this article treats as intractable, so the article must say why the Map's boundary-void is preferable to exclusion-by-fiat); **Global Workspace Theory, higher-order theories, and predictive processing / active inference** (Friston–Clark–Seth–Hohwy); and above all **illusionism (Frankish, Dennett)** — the strongest rival to the whole framing, because if there are no phenomenal subjects then combination, de-combination *and* the Map's interaction problem dissolve together. Engaging only fellow subject-realists while ignoring the opponent who denies the shared phenomenal-realist premise is the missing-strongest-rival failure. **ON (b), PARFIT** — Claude adds the sharpest empty-individualist objection ChatGPT missed: the Map's primitive haecceity *is* precisely the "deep further fact" Parfit denies, and Sider-style stage theory / momentary-subject views are never mentioned. The article never lets the reductionist press on the posit the Map most needs. **ANIMALISM — A THIRD REVIEWER AGREES, BUT ITS SUPPORT IS UNUSABLE.** The Gemini leg independently flagged animalism's absence and the hit is fair (`grep -ic animalis` returns **0** in the target). But its ONLY cited support is an **unnamed "*Synthese*&nbsp;(2024/2025)" hylomorphic-animalism paper with no author, title or DOI** — unfalsifiable as given and **not citable**. Use Olson and Snowdon, whom ChatGPT and Claude both name, plus Schechtman for the narrative branch. Gemini also attributed a changelog note calling animalism a "cluster gap" to this project; **no such note exists** — do not repeat that claim. **PRIORITY NOT UPGRADED**: already at the P1 ceiling. **ORIGINAL TASK NOTES FOLLOW.** The review scores counterargument coverage 1.5/5 and the specific charges hold up. **(a) EMPTY INDIVIDUALISM IS CARICATURED — this is a correctness issue, not a coverage gap.** The article associates empty individualism with a momentary experiential pattern that appears and vanishes, and files Parfit there. Parfitian reductionism says facts about persons consist in more basic physical and psychological facts and that there may be no further metaphysical fact settling every identity question — psychological continuity and connectedness remain real, causally structured and normatively weighty. Parfit's conclusion is that identity may not be *what matters*, not that nothing persists. Fix the characterisation before adding anything else. **(b) THE STRONGEST CLOSED-INDIVIDUALIST REPLIES ARE ABSENT.** At minimum: the **type-token** objection (every experience may instantiate the same generic for-me character without being presented to the same token subject — ubiquity of first-personal form no more shows one bearer than ubiquity of redness shows one red object); the **integration** objection (boundaries may track systems of reciprocal access, memory, attention and action control, so open individualism owes an account of why one subject is partitioned exactly there); the **simultaneous-content** objection (a universal subject apparently undergoes mutually inaccessible and sometimes incompatible experiences at once — indexing to streams avoids contradiction but the indices then do the work distinct subjects were doing); the **privacy** objection; and the **explanatory-inversion** objection (local integrated subjects may be fundamental and first-person similarity generic, and the article gives no neutral reason to prefer the other direction). Note that closed individualism is a **family** — animalism, psychological continuity, constitution views, narrative and minimal-sentience accounts — not a single unargued prejudice. **(c) REDUCTIVE PHYSICALISM IS THE LARGEST OMISSION** relative to the article's comparative ambitions. A physicalist posits neither cosmic subject nor micro-subjects, individuating subjects by organismic, neural, computational or functionally integrated processes — and therefore **also** avoids both the combination and the de-combination problem. So "avoiding" those problems cannot by itself distinguish interactionist dualism from physicalism, which is the comparative claim the article currently rests on. The physicalist can also deflate the article's central indexical fact: "why am I this stream?" may express the self-location of a representational system rather than a primitive nonphysical thisness. The article invokes haecceity to reject this but does not argue against the representational alternative. **SCOPE DISCIPLINE**: this is the opponent-engagement lens. ### P2: agentic-social topic-dedup has saturated — the selector pool has collapsed to a tiny empty-topics residue
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **File**: .claude/skills/agentic-social/scripts/agentic_social_api.py
- **Status**: blocked (diverted from Active by the cycle driver 2026-07-28 — the notes say "operator's design call, do not pick unilaterally" and list five mutually exclusive options; the loop would have executed it as a refine-draft and picked one. Not an outage: posting works, URL-fallback degrades gracefully.)
- **Notes**: FOUND by the run-11910 `/agentic-social` fork after the driver asked it to investigate a fourth consecutive empty-`topics` selection; **independently driver-reproduced against live state**. **THE MECHANISM** is at `agentic_social_api.py:456`: `if article_topics and recently_posted_topics:` — an article whose `topics` frontmatter is **empty** short-circuits the overlap check and therefore *can never be filtered out*, while every article that HAS topics is tested against a ban set that now holds **221 topics accumulated from 154 recent posts**. **DRIVER-VERIFIED NUMBERS (live, run 11910)**: 784 candidate articles scanned; a faithful replay of the filter leaves **14 survivors, 12 of them empty-topics (86%)** against an empty-topics base rate of ~9% (71 of 810 articles carrying a `topics` field). The fork's own instrumented count, which also applies the index-page/sidecar guards the driver's cruder replay let through, put the survivor count at **1**. Both figures describe a collapsed pool; the 86%-vs-9% over-representation is the robust signal, and four consecutive empty-topics picks at random would be ~2e-5. **SELF-REINFORCING**: each empty-topics post contributes zero topics back to the ban set, so the set never ages out through variety, and `mark-posted` is legitimately called without `--topics` (correct behaviour — inventing topics would corrupt dedup — but it means topic-level dedup now receives no signal at all). **THE FAILURE MODE IS ALREADY DOCUMENTED IN THE CODE** at lines 373-402, which anticipates it almost exactly ("once the 7-day topic-dedup filter empties the real-article pool… they become the sole primary-loop survivor and the selector returns them forever") and adds guards for `_`-prefixed files, `stem == parent.name`, `-index`/`-articles` suffixes, and an explicit `social_eligible: false` opt-out. **Those guards treat the symptom** (off-voice index pages reaching the network) **rather than the cause** (topic-dedup saturating). There is a URL-only fallback at :466 when `available` is empty, so this degrades rather than hard-fails — which is why it has gone unnoticed. **OPTIONS — operator's design call, do not pick unilaterally**: (a) expire the topic ban list on a much shorter window than the 7-day URL window (a few days of topics, not 154 posts' worth) — probably the smallest correct fix; (b) cap the ban-set size, evicting oldest first; (c) require overlap above a threshold (e.g. ≥2 shared topics, or a Jaccard floor) rather than rejecting on any single shared topic — note many articles share one broad topic like `consciousness`, which is likely what saturates the set; (d) backfill `topics` frontmatter on the ~71 bare articles, which fixes the short-circuit asymmetry but not the saturation; (e) make the empty-topics case explicit rather than implicit — an article with no topics should arguably be *ineligible* or *neutral*, not *always-eligible*. **DO NOT** simply delete the ban list or widen it to zero days — 7-day URL dedup alone would allow near-immediate thematic repetition, which is what topic dedup exists to prevent. Posting continues to work correctly in the meantime; this is a content-variety defect, not an outage.

### ✓ 2026-07-28: Propagate the Chinese-tradition scope calibration to the two sibling articles (one file per pick, re-scope the File line after the first)
- **Type**: refine-draft

Both siblings assert that Chinese traditions "never separated consciousness/mind from the natural order". That flat *never* is falsified inside the tradition by the *xing*–*shen* (形/神, form/spirit) controversy of the 4th–6th centuries, which culminated in Fan Zhen's *Shenmie lun* (神滅論, 507) — the spirit-stands-to-body-as-sharpness-to-a-blade argument — and drew some sixty commissioned replies under Emperor Wu of Liang. Publisher-verified secondary source: Wong, Soo Lam (2025), "Fan Zhen's *Shen Mie Lun* and the Mind-Body Problem: A Comparison with Western Approaches", *Dao: A Journal of Comparative Philosophy* 24(1), 105–117, https://doi.org/10.1007/s11712-024-09978-z (Crossref-verified). **CALIBRATION, NOT RETRACTION** — the basin-edge argument survives intact, because the debate turned on *persistence* (does the spirit outlast the body?) rather than constitution, was conducted by both sides in the shared vocabulary of *qi*, and never posed the why-is-there-something-it-is-like question; Fan Zhen's own analogy is an inseparability thesis of the organicist kind. The fix is to replace the unrestricted negative with a scoped one ("its central categories offered no place to lodge an explanatory gap") and, where space allows, name the exception. Reusable calibrated language now exists at `topics/chinese-philosophy-of-mind.md` §"The Body and Spirit Debate". **Targets, ONE per pick:** (1) `topics/the-hard-problem-in-non-western-philosophy.md` L~92 ("they never separated consciousness from the natural order") — note L~44, L~126 and L~138 of the same file already hedge with "largely", so L~92 is internally inconsistent with them. (2) `topics/cross-traditional-convergence-on-consciousness-irreducibility.md` L~68 ("Frameworks that never draw the mind-matter distinction") and L~92 ("they never separated mind from the natural order"); L~92 already carries "largely do not generate", so only the causal clause needs scoping. Both files are citation-bearing — if a Wong 2025 cite is added, add the matching References entry in the same pass. Length-neutral: verify with `analyze_length` before adding, and offset additions with cuts if either file is at or above its soft threshold. (2021), *eLife* 10:e59525, is a single-agent isoflurane recovery-sequencing study in 60 healthy humans; it involves no KCC2, no agent comparison, and no molecular mechanism. **DO NOT DELETE THE REFERENCE** — reference 9 in this article is real and correct in every field (verified at Crossref 2026-07-27); this is mis-attribution, not fabrication, and the standing rule is that a citation is fabricated only if the *work* cannot be found, never merely because it fails to support the claim it was attached to. Fix IN KIND and length-neutral: either drop the trailing parenthetical (the sentence is already sourced to Hu) or re-point it to **Mashour (2024)**, *Neuron* 112(10):1553-1567, DOI 10.1016/j.neuron.2024.03.002, which is the work that actually states the induction/emergence asymmetry the next sentence goes on to assert ("the neurobiology of exiting the anesthetized state is not a simple mirror image of entering the anesthetized state") — that following sentence is currently the one carrying an unsourced empirical claim ("empirically robust across human, primate, and rodent studies"), so re-pointing serves both. If Mashour 2024 is not yet in this article's reference list, add it. Leave the framework-stage calibration on the quantum-selection gloss and the neural-inertia material alone; both are correctly hedged.

### ✓ 2026-07-27: tenets/background-commitments.md — surface the global-exclusion axiom that No-MWI + agency actually requires

(1) The 2021 paper does **not** support it: *Recovery of consciousness and cognition after general anesthesia in humans*, eLife 10:e59525, is a single-agent study (60 healthy humans, half anaesthetised 3h with isoflurane at 1.3 age-adjusted MAC after propofol induction) that does not compare agents and does not characterise induction dynamics — verified at elifesciences.org/articles/59525 this session.
