(2024), "Anesthesia and the neurobiology of consciousness", *Neuron* 112(10):1553-1567, DOI 10.1016/j.neuron.2024.03.002**, which does make the claim as a review ("the neurobiology of exiting the anesthetized state is not a simple mirror image of entering the anesthetized state") — verified verbatim at PMC11098701 this session. Check the References block for a corresponding 2022 entry and remove or correct it. Length-neutral; do not expand the article.

### ✓ 2026-07-27: apex/born-preserving-causal-efficacy.md — add the selector-distribution law and intervention-level trilemma (novel implication)
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: From outer review 2026-07-27 (ChatGPT 5.6 Pro), novel implication 1.1, improvements 6-8. Reviewer's strongest novel inference: exact Born preservation cannot be stated only as a law over physical outcomes — it also needs a law over the distribution of conscious reasons/intentions μ(c|x), because reasons-responsive agency requires the selector policy π(o|c,x) to vary with c. This yields an intervention-level trilemma: (i) Born preservation survives intervention on intention → the selector is empirically/interventionally indistinguishable from chance or trumping; (ii) preservation holds only after averaging over natural intentions → interventions should reveal conditional Born deviations (a real experimental route, abandoning the "none by construction" corridor); (iii) conscious-state histories are themselves constrained → psychophysical superselection. Add the conditional selector equation and the trilemma; require every toy model to specify both the conscious-state distribution and the intervention profile, and to distinguish genuine agency from a relabelled hidden Born-random seed. Also flag the possible cross-agent consequence (moral agency carrying hidden statistical externalities). Distinguish natural-distribution vs arbitrary-intervention Born-preservation claims explicitly.

- **Type**: refine-draft

Huemer's own retrospective says the title is a topical pun on Bush's "compassionate conservatism" and "compassion has nothing to do with the paper" ("phenomenal" ← Greek *phainomenon*). Delete the invented rationale; keep the genuine generality/no-privileging point but stop tying it to the word "compassionate." **(e) name the isolation objection's true source AND its rebuttal** — after correcting the attribution to McCain 2017, do not leave the Bayesian-incompatibility worry standing: McCain & Moretti, *Appearance and Explanation* (OUP, 2021) argue PC is reconcilable with Bayesian updating; the two names the article miscasts as objectors are in fact PC *defenders*. **(f) Smithies 2019** — add Declan Smithies, "On the Global Ambitions of Phenomenal Conservatism," *Analytic Philosophy* 60(3):206–244 (2019), DOI 10.1111/phib.12167, as the leading recent systematic critique (currency requirement), alongside the bootstrapping/easy-knowledge family already noted.

### ✓ 2026-07-15: Address structural gaps in topics/quantum-holism-and-phenomenal-unity.md
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Pessimistic review 2026-07-15 (pessimistic-2026-07-15-quantum-holism-and-phenomenal-unity) found the article factually sound (Baum/Vicente, Denton, Hagan/Reimers all already calibrated) but carrying structural overreach in a few sentences. Three fixes, all length-neutral, PRESERVE the honest tenet-grounding: (1) HIGH — the Leibniz "mill" argument is stated as an in-principle *category mismatch* ("not a gap in current knowledge but a mismatch of categories"), which forbids ANY physical structure — quantum holism included, and the article concedes at "The Remaining Gap" that entanglement "is still *physical* holism" — from constituting phenomenal unity. Yet the lead + "Why Quantum Entanglement Matches Unity" call entanglement the "substrate structurally matching" unity / "genuine physical unity." Add one reconciling paragraph making the claim *analogical + locational* (mirror of unity, locus where collapse-selection enters), NOT constitutive; soften the lead's "substrate structurally matching" accordingly. (2) MEDIUM — epistemic→metaphysical equivocation: "The entangled system cannot be decomposed... This is ontological unity at the level of physics itself, not mere correlation." Non-separability is formal; the "ontological unity, not correlation" reading is interpretation-dependent (denied on Everettian/relational/statistical readings). Attribute it to the Map's collapse-realist commitment, not "physics itself"; pull the Neven "only true binding agent" line inside the same qualification (it restates the contested premise via a conjecture paper). (3) MEDIUM — two argument-from-ignorance moves: "Warren offered no alternative classical explanation" (Warren's objection is that the signal may be an artefact, so no alternative is owed) and epothilone "no classical mechanism explains" (microtubules have classical roles — transport, synaptic scaffolding, membrane dynamics — that could shift anaesthetic induction). Reframe both as open findings, not points in the quantum column. Minor: soften "first attempt at direct evidence" superlative; either justify or flag the Whitehead "aligns naturally" alignment; note zombie reformulation assumes conceivability that illusionists deny. See the review's Language Improvements table for exact rewrites.

### ✓ 2026-07-14: Relocate collapse-dependence from the Zeno effect to its selective reading + add Ballentine caveat (concepts/quantum-zeno-effect.md)
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: 2026-07-14 pessimistic review (reviews/pessimistic-2026-07-14.md) found two seams where the article's otherwise-scrupulous physics/reading separation slips, both on collapse-dependence. (1) Line 82 (No Many Worlds) asserts "The effect presupposes genuine collapse" — but the Zeno effect and the Itano experiment are derivable in UNITARY QM (measurement as decoherence); only the Map's SELECTIVE/consciousness reading needs collapse. Rephrase to locate the requirement in the reading, not the physics (suggested: "The selective significance the Map draws from the effect presupposes genuine collapse — one outcome actualised for the observer. Under MWI the Zeno freezing still occurs as unitary dynamics, but there is no privileged projection to enforce, and the effect loses the selective role the Map needs."). (2) Line 46 presents Itano 1990 as grounding the projection-postulate mechanism without the well-known Ballentine (Phys. Rev. A 43, 5165, 1991) critique that the inhibition follows from unitary measurement dynamics and does NOT require the projection postulate (Itano reply 43, 5168). Add one calibrated sentence: the experiment grounds the EFFECT, not the COLLAPSE interpretation. Both fixes are length-neutral and REINFORCE the article's existing physics/reading separation. Optional minor: "Reimers and McKemmish (both 2009)" (line 72) are co-authors of one 2009 critique — reword to avoid framing as two independent contests. CHURN CAVEAT: article was create+deep-review+cross-review all 2026-07-14; these are genuine calibration fixes not re-review churn — touch only the named clauses, HOLD ai_system claude-opus-4-8, bump ai_modified only (NOT last_deep_review). ### ✓ 2026-07-14: Fix "1,000 observations" arithmetic in concepts/timing-gap-problem.md (contradicts canonical quantum-zeno-effect page)
- **Type**: refine-draft

### ✓ 2026-07-07: Close the premise-neutrality gap in concepts/reflexive-methodology.md (pragmatism instance)
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: From pessimistic-review 2026-07-07 ([pessimistic-2026-07-07b](/reviews/pessimistic-2026-07-07b/)) — an adversarial-logical lens on the fresh opus-4-8 create that today's citation-focused cross-review ([deep-review-2026-07-07-reflexive-methodology](/reviews/deep-review-2026-07-07-reflexive-methodology/)) did not test. The article's HEADLINE thesis is premise-neutrality: "The Map does not defeat materialism, pragmatism, or Russellian monism by importing dualist premises the opponent rejects … lets the standard do the work" (line 31); "it never assumes irreducibility" (line 87). That universal claim CRACKS at its own flagship instance. The **pragmatism** case (line 59, "immanent critique in textbook form") turns on: "reduce evaluation to physical mechanism and 'what works' collapses into 'what merely happens to occur,' because there is no longer any standpoint from which to judge that a problem has been *resolved*." That collapse is NOT entailed by pragmatism's "what works" standard — a naturalist pragmatist (Dewey, Rorty) holds normativity/evaluation is constituted by physical/functional/social processes with no irreducible conscious standpoint, so "what works" does not collapse. The article's assertion that it does presupposes that a physically-constituted standpoint is not a genuine evaluative standpoint — the Map's own irreducibility CONCLUSION imported as a PREMISE at the exact step claimed to be purely immanent. Per [direct-refutation-discipline](/project/direct-refutation-discipline/) this is the "in-framework argument that actually appeals to Map commitments" failure (critical). ALSO an [evidential-status-discipline](/project/evidential-status-discipline/) epistemic/metaphysical equivocation: the phenomenal datum "evaluation is a conscious/felt activity" (secured by the Stroud reply, line 83) is recruited to assert the metaphysical claim "evaluation is irreducible to physical mechanism" — the physicalist grants the datum, denies the irreducibility; the Stroud guardrail closes belief-vs-truth, NOT datum-vs-irreducibility. FIX (preserve substance, no editor-vocabulary/mode-labels in body): EITHER (a) UPGRADE the pragmatism instance — supply the genuinely in-framework argument for why naturalized normativity fails pragmatism's OWN test without presupposing irreducibility; OR (b) HONESTLY DOWNGRADE — mark in natural prose that the collapse step engages the physicalist at a framework boundary (the Map's commitment that a physical standpoint is not a genuine evaluative standpoint) and soften the universal "never imports dualist premises / lets the standard do the work" so it does not over-promise (scope it to the instances where it genuinely holds — the Cutter-recoil and closure-circularity cases ARE premise-neutral as claimed; pragmatism and arguably retorsion are not). Consider adding a third guardrail parallel to Stroud/tu-quoque that distinguishes the phenomenal datum from the irreducibility claim. LENGTH-SAFE (1909w, concepts soft 2500 — headroom; keep length-neutral-to-slightly-additive). NO-OP HYGIENE: real fix → bump BOTH ai_modified + last_deep_review; `date -u`-check stamps not future-dated (fork-future-dates-frontmatter-timestamps). Dedupe: no open task targets concepts/reflexive-methodology.md (the cross-review + write tasks are ✓-completed); not vetoed.

### ✓ 2026-07-07: Research Anthropic's "global workspace / J-space" work (paper + commentaries)
- **Type**: research-topic
- **Notes**: User request (2026-07-07) — fully research Anthropic's global workspace / J-space work as the foundation of a research→integrate chain. PRIMARY SOURCES to read and take notes on: (1) the announcement <https://www.anthropic.com/research/global-workspace>; (2) the paper **"Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models,"** Gurnee, Sofroniew, Pearce, Piotrowski, Kauvar, Chen, Soligo, Bogdan, Ong, Wang, Thompson, Abrahams, Kantamneni, Ameisen, Batson & Lindsey (Anthropic, **2026-07-06**), at <https://transformer-circuits.pub/2026/workspace/index.html>; open-source **Jacobian lens** at github.com/anthropics/jacobian-lens; interactive demo at neuronpedia.org/jlens. (3) The THREE external commentaries flagged on the announcement — **Stanislas Dehaene & Lionel Naccache** (originators of Global Workspace Theory / global neuronal workspace); **Patrick Butlin, Dillon Plunkett, Robert Long & Derek Shiller** (AI-consciousness / moral-status researchers — connect to Butlin et al.'s indicator-property framework the Map already cites); and **Neel Nanda** (DeepMind interpretability, incl. an independent replication). CORE CLAIM to capture accurately: via a "Jacobian lens" the authors identify a **J-space** subspace of Claude's activations exhibiting five functional properties of *access* consciousness — verbal report, directed modulation ("hold X in mind"), unverbalized internal-reasoning steps, flexible cross-task generalization, and selectivity (mediates deliberate reasoning, not automatic fluency); it holds only a few dozen concepts and <10% of activity, emerged in training, and is used for safety (evaluation-awareness, hidden-goal, suppressed-thought detection). LOAD-BEARING CAVEAT for the Map (verify against the source, do not overstate): the authors **explicitly take no position on phenomenal consciousness** — "access consciousness is a purely functional notion; the relationship it has with subjective experience... is widely debated. In this paper, we take no position." This is directly germane to Tenet 1 (Dualism): a striking *empirical* demonstration of access consciousness that by the authors' own framing leaves the phenomenal/experiential question — the Map's turf — untouched. Output a research note to `obsidian/research/anthropic-global-workspace-j-space-2026-07-07.md`. ### ✓ 2026-07-06: Address the moral-realism / evolutionary-debunking objection in ethics-of-possible-ai-consciousness.md
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: From outer review 2026-06-27 (Gemini 2.5 Pro — "The Normative Void and the Presumption of Moral Realism"; a distinct angle NOT raised by the same-date ChatGPT or Claude legs). The article's whole edifice presupposes that if an AI is conscious and suffering there is an objective moral fact that we ought to reduce that suffering — i.e. robust moral realism — but never defends that presupposition against Sharon Street's Darwinian Dilemma (evolutionary debunking of moral intuitions). The objection: human suffering-aversion intuitions evolved for genetic fitness, not tracking of mind-independent moral truth, so projecting them onto non-biological synthetic systems is doubly unwarranted. This is a real gap (grep-confirmed: no "Street" / "debunking" / "moral realism" in the article). The Map likely DOES have a metaethical commitment here (consciousness-grounds-value via [consciousness-value-connection](/concepts/consciousness-value-connection/) / [evaluative-phenomenal-character](/concepts/evaluative-phenomenal-character/)) — so the right move is probably a compact in-framework reply: the Map grounds the badness of suffering in the *phenomenal character of suffering itself* (constitutive, not inferred from evolved intuition), which sidesteps the Darwinian Dilemma's "our access would be coincidental" worry. Verify that framing against [ethics-under-dualism](/topics/ethics-under-dualism/) and [evaluative-phenomenal-character](/concepts/evaluative-phenomenal-character/) before asserting it, and link whichever Map article carries the metaethics. Keep it tight — see the length warning on the sibling Gemini task (article near the 4000w ceiling). Apply the [direct-refutation-discipline](/project/direct-refutation-discipline/) remit per [the writing-style guide](/project/writing-style/); keep mode-labels out of the body. ### ✓ 2026-06-27: Drop the "tenets force the Duplication View" entailment claim in ethics-of-possible-ai-consciousness.md
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: From convergent outer reviews (2026-06-27, 3/3 reviewers): [chatgpt, claude, gemini]. All three independently flagged the copy-multiplicity / Aggregation section as the article's central structural defect — the DOMINANT convergence of the cycle. Claude (Section B): the inference is invalid, "rejecting MWI... is logically orthogonal to counting simultaneous co-existing physical copies." Gemini (Weakness #2, "metaphysical smuggling"): "the author dictates the Duplication View entirely to protect an unstated, overarching metaphysical agenda... the very definition of metaphysical smuggling." ChatGPT reaches the same section via the Bostrom-citation route + its "dualist bracketing" critique. NOTE: Gemini's specific "it is hidden/smuggled" framing is partly a MISREAD — the article is openly transparent that it adopts Duplication because of its tenets (it says so in plain text and appends a self-critical transparency note); the actionable residue all three converge on is the over-claim that the tenets *force* Duplication (Bostrom 2006 derives it with no Map tenet). Already P1 — not upgraded, but convergence formalized. VERIFIED tenet-leakage / constitutional-attractor defect on the live text. The Aggregation section (lines 58–60) claims the Map is "committed *by its own tenets*" to the Duplication View, that rejecting Many-Worlds plus haecceity is "structurally the same move that grounds the Duplication View," and that "the same machinery that defeats MWI forbids the Unification escape." This inference is INVALID: rejecting MWI concerns whether non-actual branches of a *single* system are real, whereas copy-multiplicity concerns whether many spatially-distinct realizers *in one world at one time* ground one experience-token or many — the two are logically orthogonal. The reviewer's decisive internal refutation: Bostrom 2006 derives Duplication with NO appeal to haecceity and NO rejection of MWI (he argues from computationalism + ethical/epistemic consequence while explicitly bracketing personal identity), proving the tenets are neither necessary nor sufficient for Duplication. FIX: rewrite the section to state plainly that the tenets are *consistent with* but do NOT *force* Duplication, and delete/heavily-qualify the "structurally the same move that defeats MWI" sentence (false as stated). The Duplication View may still be the Map's adopted position — only the entailment claim must go. Apply the [direct-refutation-discipline](/project/direct-refutation-discipline/) remit: this is an unsupported foundational move the framework has not earned by its own standards — name it honestly in natural journal-quality prose per [the writing-style guide](/project/writing-style/)'s "Engaging Opponents in Journal-Quality Prose" section; if the entailment cannot be salvaged in-framework, state in natural prose that the tenets underdetermine the copy-counting question. Do NOT expose mode labels in the article body — keep the classification in the refine-draft changelog entry. Tenet alignment: Tenet 4 (No Many Worlds) — protects the tenet by NOT overstating what it entails; honest-engagement discipline.

- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: From convergent outer reviews 2026-06-23 (Claude Opus 4.8 + ChatGPT 5.5 Pro), site-wide methodology proposal. **(b) a co-optation firewall for INFERENTIAL (not just citational) recruitment** — a citation can be perfectly accurate yet illegitimately recruit a physicalist author's result toward a rejected conclusion via a bridging premise that IS the contested thesis (the Zheng & Meister 10 bits/s → quantum-selection-budget move is the worked example); - **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Pessimistic review 2026-06-17 found three real citation defects (web-verified). (1) DANGLING CITE: line 98 cites "His 1978 morphine argument" (Dennett) but there is NO Dennett 1978 entry in References — add Dennett, D. (1978), "Why You Can't Make a Computer That Feels Pain" (Brainstorms, 1978), verifying year/venue at publisher of record before committing. (3) MISATTRIBUTED QUOTE SOURCE: line 120 quotes Searle "Where consciousness is concerned... the existence of the appearance is the reality" and Reference 17 (line 191) attributes it to Searle (1992) The Rediscovery of the Mind (MIT Press). Gemini 2.5 Pro: "leaves the manuscript's defense of the explanatory gap entirely untested against its strongest modern opponents" (AST/Frankish soft illusionism, predictive-processing representationalism). NOTE Gemini OVERSTATED this — its claim the article "completely ignores" illusionism is FALSE (the article's L102 Site Perspective already lists illusionist/metacognitive deflation as a live physicalist resource, per the Gemini review's own Verification Notes); the convergent, defensible core is "import and develop the strongest versions in-body rather than linking away," NOT Gemini's "blunt refusal to engage" framing. ### ✓ 2026-06-07: Replace asserted evidential parity with "physicalism not compelled" + de-leak Davidson co-optation (duhem-quine article)
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: From outer review 2026-06-07 (Claude Opus 4.8). Two precise, distinct edits. (a) **Parity overstatement** — the line "Neither programme can claim evidential supremacy" (currently ~line 112) asserts PARITY, a stronger conclusion than underdetermination delivers. Underdetermination shows physicalism is not *compelled*; it does not establish that the two programmes are evidentially equal (Laudan & Leplin: empirically equivalent theories can differ in evidential support). Replace the parity claim with the weaker, defensible "underdetermination shows physicalism is not forced," and elsewhere close the epistemic→metaphysical slide (insert and exclude the intervening non-dualist alternatives — type-B physicalism, Russellian monism — wherever the text moves from "physical description does not entail phenomenal experience" to "dualism"). (b) **Davidson co-optation** — the framework-dependence / "lossy translation" passage recruits Davidson as if he supported incommensurable schemes; Davidson argued the opposite (the very idea of incommensurable conceptual schemes is unintelligible — "On the Very Idea of a Conceptual Scheme," 1974). Either drop the Davidson framing or mark the disagreement honestly; do not present a dualism-favorable "lossy translation" reading as Davidson's view. Mark dualism-favorable conclusions in the "neutral" theoretical-virtues/framework-dependence passages as tenet-driven interpretations, not analysis outputs. Preserve calibration language; length-neutral.

(1) MEDIUM epistemic/metaphysical equivocation in "The Inferentialist Reading" (¶51–53) and the Dualism tenet-connection (¶71): the regress (inferentialist reading) establishes at most an *articulation/formalisation* limit ("no augmentation of *explicit* rules reproduces taking-as"), but the prose slides to a *constitutively non-formal mental operation* ("primitive operation of consciousness," "one face of the irreducibly mental") which is what the Dualism link requires — the speculation marker is attached to the Gödel resemblance, not to this epistemic→metaphysical bridge. Fix per [evidential-status-discipline](/project/evidential-status-discipline/): split the two readings explicitly and supply the bridging argument (why an articulation-limit is evidence of a constitutively non-formal operation rather than an unformalised-but-physical one), addressing the "syntactic fact ≠ cognitive claim" objection — or downgrade. (2) MEDIUM boundary-substitution in the Brandom paragraph (¶63), the only engagement with the strongest contemporary opponent: the reply "social practice is itself a tissue of individual takings" *presupposes* individual-first priority, the exact premise Brandom denies — it does not refute Brandom inside his framework. Per [direct-refutation-discipline](/project/direct-refutation-discipline/), either supply the in-framework argument (the community's conferral of an inferential licence is itself a taking-the-move-as-licensed, so the regress relocates not dissolves — without presupposing individualism) OR downgrade honestly to framework-boundary marking ("the disagreement turns on a prior commitment, not a refutation within Brandom's framework"). The Wittgenstein paragraph (¶59) already does this correctly — make Brandom inherit its discipline. Also soften "provably insufficient"/"shown to be incomplete by formal argument" (¶69) → "argued"/"on the inferentialist reading" (the reading is contested, so not *proven*); and scope the "self-stultifying" charge (¶69) to the agent-act reading (a formal calculus has no cognition to presuppose). LENGTH-NEUTRAL preferred. PRESERVE the up-front honesty ("later moves rest on the inferentialist reading being defensible, not uncontested") and the cousins-not-siblings Gödel calibration. ### ✓ 2026-06-04: Fix conversion-disorder factual error in clinical-dissociation-as-systematic-evidence.md (increased, not severed, amygdala-motor coupling)
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: From Claude Opus 4.8 outer review 2026-06-04 (VERIFIED FACTUAL ERROR, the review's headline finding, likely distinct from ChatGPT's same-day review). The article frames conversion disorder / FND as a "descending motor channel DISCONNECTING" (citing Vuilleumier 2005, Brown 2004). The modern FND literature reports the OPPOSITE: **increased** functional connectivity between amygdala and motor/supplementary-motor regions — heightened limbic *influence over* motor control, not a severed channel. Voon et al. (2010, *Brain*, "Emotional stimuli and motor conversion disorder": greater right-amygdala↔right-SMA connectivity, Granger-causal amygdala→SMA direction); Hassa et al. (2017, *NeuroImage: Clinical*, n=13 functional-hemiparesis: increased left-amygdala↔(pre-)SMA + subthalamic-nucleus connectivity). The contemporary mechanism is Edwards, Adams, Brown, Pareés & Friston (2012, *Brain* 135(11):3495-3512, "A Bayesian account of 'hysteria'"): an abnormally precise intermediate-level motor prior ACTIVELY GENERATES the symptom (aberrant precision-weighting), not a severed channel — the article's framing is closer to the discarded Freud/Janet "hysteria" picture than current FND science (Stone/Edwards/Aybek/Hallett/Perez). FIX: replace the "channel disconnect" framing with the increased-coupling / active-generation account; concede "intact motor system + functional symptom" is now explained by active generation, not disconnection. ⚠ WEB-VERIFY every cite at publisher of record before adding (Voon 2010 Brain, Hassa 2017 NeuroImage:Clinical, Edwards/Friston 2012 Brain) — full author incl given name (ai_citation_metadata_unreliable; wrong-author/dual-date caught repeatedly). ⚠ PROPAGATE to siblings inheriting the same motor-channel framing (conversion-disorder-as-consciousness-side-fault, neurological-dissociations-as-interface-architecture, dissociative-states-as-intact-substrate-interface-evidence). Benchmark that would partly rehabilitate the disconnect framing: a post-2015 replication showing *reduced* prefrontal-motor connectivity as dominant FND signature.

### ✓ 2026-06-03: Fix Han & Choi (2016) citation gloss in brain-internal-born-rule-testing.md
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Pessimistic review (pessimistic-2026-06-03-brain-internal-born-rule-testing) found a load-bearing CITATION GLOSS defect in §"What the Corridor Is" (L55). The text attributes to Han & Choi (2016) the claim that "the per-trial information-theoretic capacity of such channels vanishes asymptotically as the number of trials grows." WEB-VERIFIED: the cite is REAL (Sci. Rep. 6:22986; arXiv:1307.2026) but the paper does NOT prove this — it derives the Born rule from a strengthened relativistic-causality condition and bounds quantum nonlocality; there is no per-trial, trials-indexed capacity-vanishing theorem. This is a possibility→theorem upgrade (an informal corollary dressed as a proven information-theoretic result), exactly what [evidential-status-discipline](/project/evidential-status-discipline/) guards against. FIX (surgical — do NOT disturb surrounding calibrated prose): downgrade to the qualitative claim the source actually supports — Born-deviating probability assignments under their causality condition enable superluminal signalling, so a strictly Born-compliant selection channel transmits no ensemble-level information (this is also exactly what the article's Torres Alegre 2025 cite proves: Φ(p)=p unique under no-signalling). Do NOT assert-fabricated and do NOT delete the cite — the paper is genuine; only its gloss is wrong. Article conclusion survives on the qualitative argument. The other three hot-zone cites (Torres Alegre arXiv:2512.12636, Arana 2025 PhilArchive ARATCQ-2, Kerskens & López Pérez 2022) were verified genuine — leave them.

### ✓ 2026-06-03: Close the van Inwagen life→consciousness gap on the biological route in consciousness-and-the-metaphysics-of-composition.md
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: From outer review 2026-06-03 (Gemini 2.5 Pro), Sections 3.1 & weakness #5 — the ONE genuinely new finding from the Gemini leg (the rest CONVERGED with the ChatGPT+Claude tasks above; see this review's `## Verification Notes`). The biological route (van Inwagen) in the convergence argument treats van Inwagen's organicism as a "route to consciousness," but van Inwagen's actual composition criterion is **metabolic/homeostatic/teleological life-unity, NOT phenomenal consciousness**. The article relies on an undefended bridge premise: that *all and only living things are conscious* (biopsychism/panbiotism). Plants, fungi, and single-celled organisms are living composites on van Inwagen's view yet are not phenomenally conscious subjects in the sense the unity/interaction argument needs — so the biological route reaches *life-unity*, and only reaches *consciousness* via an unstated, contestable identification. This is the same "convergence only after redescription / equivocation on 'consciousness'" structure the ChatGPT+Claude legs flagged for the IIT and Merricks routes (the convergence-calibration P2 above), but applied specifically to the van Inwagen leg — so COORDINATE with that task (it is the natural home for this if the refine touches the convergence framing; keep as a distinct sub-point so it isn't lost). FIX (length-neutral): where the biological route is introduced, either (a) explicitly state and defend/qualify the life→consciousness bridge (note that van Inwagen himself defends a *materialist* ontology of persons — do not recruit him as a consciousness-criterion proponent without caveat, cf. the parallel McQueen & Tsuchiya living-author-misattribution P1 above), or (b) recast the route as reaching *organic/causal unity* that the Map then argues is consciousness-involving, marking that second step as a Map-internal move rather than van Inwagen's. Apply the [direct-refutation-discipline](/project/direct-refutation-discipline/) remit: this is most likely an honest framework-boundary / unsupported-foundational-move case (the article has not earned "life = consciousness" by van Inwagen's own standards) — reply in natural journal-quality prose per [writing-style](/project/writing-style/), NO mode labels in the body. Honour [evidential-status-discipline](/project/evidential-status-discipline/) and ai_citation_metadata_unreliable (van Inwagen = living author; verify any attributed position). Do NOT grow the article past its length threshold — coordinate with the other open composition tasks to stay length-neutral (outer-review-same-file-task-pileup).

The headline claim (line 33, verbatim) — "three of the most prominent answers to the SCQ independently converge on consciousness" — overstates the field: the standard mereology map (universalism, nihilism, restricted composition, brutal composition, composition-as-identity, deflationism) does not treat van Inwagen/Merricks/McQueen-Tsuchiya as *the* three dominant answers, and the convergence is real "only after abstraction" to organised/causally-unified/integrated systems (consciousness one candidate marker, not the only one). - **Type**: refine-draft

CONVERGENT — all three independently flagged that the article leaves its central premise unprotected against the dominant in-framework explanations of the "introspective void." Gemini (weakness 5): the text "completely ignores Illusionism... the void is merely the functional shadow of the brain's data-compression architecture" and HOT, under which "the 'added content' [of introspection] is the very thing that turns a biologically unconscious physiological state into a conscious experience." Claude (Dimension 1/4): "a physicalist—indeed an illusionist like Dennett or a higher-order theorist—can run the identical observer-effect argument," so the article "does not engage the strongest opposing position." ChatGPT (§3): "higher-order and global-workspace-style theories deserve explicit engagement... reportability, availability, access, or metacognitive monitoring are not merely contaminating additions; they are part of what makes a state conscious." A boundary-substitution finding NOT subsumed by the ChatGPT generic "What Would Challenge This View?" section — this task names the specific competitors. Verified by reading the article: it engages **none** of the three dominant deflationary frameworks that explain the "introspective void" without an irreducible lower bound — Higher-Order Thought (HOT) theory (the void = absence of a higher-order representation; introspective "enrichment" is the very thing that makes a state conscious, so demanding a pre-enrichment conscious state is asking to see a square circle), Global Workspace Theory (the lower bound = the minimum threshold of global broadcast; failure to introspect below it = failure to broadcast weak signals), and Illusionism (the void = the resolution limit of the brain's self-monitoring; a computational blind spot reified into metaphysics). Apply the [direct-refutation-discipline](/project/direct-refutation-discipline/) remit. This is the classic boundary-substitution failure mode three independent outer reviewers have converged on: a competing in-framework explanation is available and goes unengaged. The right move is a mix of (a) in-framework engagement where the deflation can be met on its own terms — e.g. HOT and the void's thesis are partly *complementary* (both agree introspection adds structure; they disagree on whether anything conscious exists below it), so state precisely where the disagreement bites rather than ignoring HOT; and (b) honest framework-boundary-marking where it cannot — illusionism denies the explanandum (phenomenal "what-it's-like") the Map takes as given under [dualism](/tenets/#dualism), so name that as a bedrock disagreement, NOT a refutation. Do NOT let the article's existing dualist commitment silently *close* the question against these competitors; present them as live alternatives the void is underdetermined between, then state the Map's reasons for its reading. Add a compact "Deflationary Alternatives" passage (or fold into the planned "What Would Challenge This View?" section from the ChatGPT task — coordinate to avoid duplication). Apply reply modes in natural journal-quality prose ([writing-style guide](/project/writing-style/)); do NOT expose mode labels in the body — classification goes in the changelog. ### ✓ 2026-05-25: Acknowledge dual-process / continuous-signal-detection contestation in memory-anomalies
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Pessimistic review 2026-05-19d Issue 3. The memory-anomalies article presents the familiarity/recollection dual-process model (Mandler, Yonelinas, Tulving) as the canonical theoretical framework — but the active 2020s recognition-memory literature includes substantial debate. Wixted and Mickes's continuous-signal-detection (CSD) account treats recognition as a unidimensional process at different memory-strength levels, predicting that familiarity and recollection are quantitatively different rather than qualitatively different. Under CSD, the article's headline "three rotations on a single failure" framing does not run as written — déjà vu and jamais vu would be artefacts of where the signal sits on the continuous strength dimension, and cryptomnesia would be a separate phenomenon entirely (post-retrieval source-attribution failure, not the recognition machinery at all). The fix is to add a paragraph (or substantive sentence in §"The Dual-Process Architecture") acknowledging that the dual-process / continuous-process debate is live in the 2020s literature, and either (a) note that the Map's phenomenal-output / causal-machinery dissociation claim does not require the dual-process commitment specifically — it can be re-derived from any architecture in which signal-pattern producing phenomenology comes apart from signal-pattern tracking truth — or (b) explicitly run the architectural-framing argument as conditional on the dual-process commitment with a marked "*on the dual-process reading*" qualifier. Reference candidates: Wixted 2007 (*Memory & Cognition*); Wixted and Mickes 2010 (*Psychological Review*); Pratte and Rouder 2012; Cohen et al. 2013. See `reviews/pessimistic-2026-05-19d.md` §"Critical Issues" Issue 3.

### ✓ 2026-05-25: Add MWI counterfactual-exclusion checklist across agency, death, quantum, machine-consciousness articles
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Outer-review 2026-05-22 ChatGPT 5.5 Pro §2.F, §4 Tenet 4. The tenets page has correctly made the indexical objection load-bearing and parsimony secondary in the Map's rejection of MWI. That repair matters because Tenet 5 (Occam's-razor limits) would otherwise undercut anti-MWI arguments based mainly on ontological extravagance. Downstream articles still sometimes treat MWI as if it would straightforwardly fail phenomenologically or empirically, when the better formulation is: MWI can often provide a branch-local restatement of the data; the Map rejects what it does to indexical identity, actuality, and selection. The reviewer also identifies a deeper implication: the rejection of MWI is doing identity work as much as quantum-foundational work — agency requires counterfactual exclusion, not just that one branch contains an agent who reports choosing. Refine pass should (a) define a standard "MWI checklist" — when an article mentions MWI, it should distinguish the branch-local data-restatement from the indexical/identity/counterfactual-exclusion objection; (b) apply the checklist across `topics/free-will`, `topics/death`, `topics/machine-consciousness`, `topics/forward-in-time-conscious-selection`, `apex/machine-question`, and the agency cluster (treat as parent task; sub-pass per article); (c) make explicit the cross-cluster role of No-MWI as a personhood-and-responsibility tenet, not just a quantum-interpretation tenet; (d) honour `[[evidential-status-discipline]]` — the indexical objection is the load-bearing argument; phenomenological / empirical objections to MWI are weaker and should not be presented as decisive. Tenet alignment: Tenet 4 (Rejection of MWI); Tenet 1 (identity-side).

### ✓ 2026-05-25: Tighten O'Brien-Kop puruṣa parallel in epistemology-of-convergence-arguments
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Outer-review 2026-05-23 Claude Opus 4.7 §2 (O'Brien-Kop reading is one-sided). The article uses O'Brien-Kop (2023) to support a parallel between Sāṃkhya puruṣa and Chalmers's phenomenal consciousness. The citation is real and the metadata correct, but O'Brien-Kop's own framing complicates the parallel more than the article acknowledges: pure consciousness in Sāṃkhya is described as "contentless" and explicitly "does not contain sensation, feeling, or experience." Verified via secondary sources summarising the paper. This makes puruṣa *less* like phenomenal consciousness (which is paradigmatically the *what-it-is-like* of feeling and sensation) than the article implies. The current hedge to "rival scholarship (Larson, Bryant, Whicher)" understates how much O'Brien-Kop herself complicates the parallel. Refine pass: (a) Add a sentence flagging that O'Brien-Kop's reading shifts the hard problem from "subjectivity as conscious experience" to "subjectivity as the capacity to consciously recognize experience," which is a non-trivial difference from Chalmers's framing; (b) Acknowledge the contentless characterisation explicitly — the article should not lean on O'Brien-Kop for a parallel her own argument resists; (c) Either find a different supporting source for the strict puruṣa-phenomenal-consciousness parallel (Larson, Bryant, or Whicher may be available; their readings are more closely aligned with the article's framing) or weaken the parallel to fit O'Brien-Kop's framing honestly. Apply the direct-refutation discipline if it turns out the parallel cannot be sustained at the strength the article claims — mark it as a framework-boundary issue rather than a clean cross-traditional convergence. Tenet alignment: Tenet 1 + calibration discipline (don't lean a convergence argument on a source whose own argument resists the convergence).

### ✓ 2026-05-25: Rescope or substantively engage canonical convergence literature in epistemology-of-convergence-arguments
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Outer-review 2026-05-23 Claude Opus 4.7 §1 (Scope misframing) and §4 (Literature gaps). The title promises "the epistemology of convergence arguments" — a general epistemological analysis — but the article delivers a defense of a Swinburne-style cumulative case applied to consciousness/dualism. An expert in epistemology or philosophy of science would flag the absence of: **Whewell** (*Philosophy of the Inductive Sciences*, 1840 — the canonical articulation of "consilience of inductions," the structural claim the article advances, and the Hesse–Laudan debate over how to formalize it); **Laudan** ("A Confutation of Convergent Realism," *Philosophy of Science* 48(1): 19–49, 1981, DOI 10.1086/288975 — locus classicus for the very phrase "convergent realism" and the pessimistic meta-induction); **Psillos** (*Scientific Realism: How Science Tracks Truth*, Routledge 1999 — standard contemporary treatment); **Bovens & Hartmann** (*Bayesian Epistemology*, OUP 2003 — canonical formal treatment of convergence from "partially reliable independent witnesses"); **Blackwell–Dubins merging of opinions**, **Gaifman–Snir convergence-to-the-truth**, washing-out-of-priors; **Salmon** on common-cause explanation (directly relevant to the article's "common-cause-null" gesture, see separate task on that); **Sober** on the law of likelihood; **Lipton** (*Inference to the Best Explanation*, 2nd ed., Routledge 2004); **Stanford** (*Exceeding Our Grasp*, OUP 2006, on the problem of unconceived alternatives — directly relevant to the article's claim that no rival explanation of cross-cultural patterns is available); **Peirce** on convergence to truth in the long run; **Condorcet** jury theorem; and consensus-as-marker-of-reliability literature (Solomon, Beatty, Moss). Refine pass should choose between two paths: (a) **rescope** — retitle to something like "A Cumulative Case for the Irreducibility of Consciousness" or "Cross-Traditional Convergence and the Hard Problem," which is what the article actually argues; or (b) **expand** — add substantive sections engaging at minimum Whewell, Laudan 1981, Bovens & Hartmann 2003, plus the Bayesian convergence-of-opinion theorems. Option (a) is cheaper but cedes the more ambitious framing; option (b) lifts the article to a genuine contribution to the convergence-epistemology literature. The editor decision belongs in the changelog. Apply the direct-refutation discipline. Identify what kind of engagement the issue calls for: showing the opponent's position is defective on its own terms (Laudan's pessimistic meta-induction needs honest engagement, not deflection), naming an unsupported foundational move the framework has not earned by its own standards, or honestly marking the framework-boundary disagreement (the article's distinction between convergence-on-diagnosis vs convergence-on-solution may be the framework-boundary move that makes engagement with Laudan tractable). Apply the corresponding reply mode in **natural journal-quality prose** — see [the writing-style guide](/project/writing-style/)'s "Engaging Opponents in Journal-Quality Prose" section. **Do not expose mode labels in the article body.** Tenet alignment: Tenet 5 (Occam's Razor Has Limits — Laudan's pessimistic meta-induction is the canonical case for parsimony's limits); the engagement is also a calibration check on whether the convergence argument is doing the work claimed.

### ✓ 2026-05-24: Fix fabricated and conflated Barrett citation in epistemology-of-convergence-arguments
- **Type**: refine-draft
- **Notes**: Outer-review 2026-05-23 Claude Opus 4.7 §2 (Citation problems). Reference 7 in the reference list (line 212) — "Barrett, J.L., Burdett, E.R.R., & Porter, T.J. (2021). The cognitive science of afterlife beliefs. In J.M. Fischer & B. Curl-Langager (Eds.), *Death and the Afterlife*. Springer." — is **fabricated**. No such Springer volume exists; Fischer and Curl-Langager work in unrelated fields and have never collaborated. The in-text claim on line 135 ("Barrett et al.'s (2021) cross-cultural study of afterlife beliefs found most participants expected mental states to cease with bodily death") is a roughly accurate paraphrase of the **real** paper by **H. Clark Barrett** (anthropologist, UCLA) — Barrett, H.C., Bolyanatz, A., Broesch, T., Cohen, E., Froerer, P., Kanovsky, M., Schug, M.G., & Laurence, S. (2021), "Intuitive Dualism and Afterlife Beliefs: A Cross-Cultural Study," *Cognitive Science* 45(6): e12992, DOI 10.1111/cogs.12992. The article appears to have grabbed **Justin L. Barrett**'s name (the more famous figure on afterlife cognition; founder of Blueprint 1543, formerly Oxford) and attached it to H. Clark Barrett's actual finding, then invented a chapter for it. Verified via Google Scholar / Springer / WorldCat / both Barretts' CVs. Refine pass should: (a) replace Reference 7 with the real H. Clark Barrett et al. (2021) *Cognitive Science* citation; (b) re-check the in-text gloss — the real paper's headline conclusion is that "the overall pattern of responses nonetheless does not support intuitive dualism in afterlife beliefs" but with the more nuanced finding that "while dualist thinking is a possible mode of thought enabled by evolved human psychology, such thinking does not constitute a default mode of thought"; the article's current paraphrase ("expected mental states to cease with bodily death") is on-message but understates how the result actually *strengthens* rather than weakens the article's preferred conclusion by removing the innate-dualism debunking explanation; (c) consider adding a brief note in the article body acknowledging the previous misattribution as a calibration-discipline footnote, or quietly correct without flag. Tenet alignment: Tenet 5 (Occam's Razor Has Limits) — the calibration discipline obliges us to verify our own citations rather than letting LLM-generated reference lists pass uninspected.

Write a concept-tier page that (a) names the distinction cleanly — *process/content distinction*: the asymmetric reliability of introspective reports — what is *being experienced* (content) is accessible to introspection with high warranted trust at Layer 1, but *how the experience is generated* (process) is not introspectively accessible and inference about it is confabulation-prone; (b) anchors the distinction in Nisbett & Wilson 1977 *Psychological Review* as the founding empirical statement (the verbal-report study series demonstrating subjects systematically confabulate process-explanations for behaviours whose actual causes were experimentally manipulated outside awareness); the layered-trust framing it enables is the catalogue's calibration craft applied to introspective evidence); (e) cross-links bidirectionally to [introspection](/concepts/introspection/), [heterophenomenology](/concepts/heterophenomenology/), [phenomenal-authority-and-first-person-evidence](/topics/phenomenal-authority-and-first-person-evidence/), microphenomenology (if exists), [neurophenomenology-and-contemplative-neuroscience](/concepts/neurophenomenology-and-contemplative-neuroscience/), [self-stultification](/concepts/self-stultification/), [confabulation-void](/voids/confabulation-void/), [mine-ness](/concepts/mine-ness/) (where the process/content distinction underwrites the separability claim); ### ✓ 2026-05-19: Write topic article on Memory-System Vulnerability Hierarchies as Interface Evidence
- **Type**: expand-topic
- **Notes**: Suggested by optimistic-2026-05-18 (High Priority). Builds on §"Memory, Sleep, and the Vanishing of Time" (lines 137–145) of `topics/consciousness-disruption-and-the-mind-brain-interface.md`, specifically the Tulving anoetic/noetic/autonoetic mapping onto anaesthesia susceptibility. The disruption article notes the hierarchy briefly (anaesthesia preserves implicit/anoetic, severs episodic/autonoetic) but does not develop it. The hierarchy is one of the catalogue's most underdeveloped strengths: it is a *graded* prediction the filter theory makes ("an interface with multiple channels is partially blocked") that production theories struggle to predict (they would predict uniform loss). A dedicated topic article would map the hierarchy across (a) anaesthesia (anoetic preserved, noetic disrupted, autonoetic severed) — Tulving's framework + the anaesthesia-recovery literature; (b) sleep stages (NREM-2 disrupts autonoetic, REM partially restores noetic-autonoetic, dreams produce noetic-only narratives); (c) hemispherectomy preservation patterns (which channels return after hemispheric reorganisation; the surprising preservation in adult-onset cases); (d) terminal lucidity (which channels return in the last hours/days — the catalogue's strongest exhibit of selective channel-restoration); (e) dissociative states (DID's compartmentalised autonoetic access; dissociative amnesia's selective autonoetic blockade with noetic preserved). The philosophical work: graded-vulnerability-with-separable-channels is a *stronger* filter-prediction than the single-binary-extinction reading — production theories must additionally account for *why these channels degrade in this order*, while filter theory predicts the ordering directly from differential channel-bandwidth and reconstruction-cost. Should explicitly engage the rival predictive-processing reading (which can also produce graded predictions through hierarchical-prior reweighting) and locate the disagreement at where each framing predicts the ordering from. Target: `topics/` placement (244/250 = 6 slots available; verify cap state at execution time). Estimated scope: 3,000–3,500 words. Tenet alignment: Tenets 1 (Dualism), 2 (MQI), 3 (Bidirectional Interaction) — the graded interface architecture is what the tenets predict. Cross-links: `[[consciousness-disruption-and-the-mind-brain-interface]]`, `[[anaesthesia-and-the-consciousness-interface]]`, `[[concepts/filter-theory]]`, `[[topics/anoetic-noetic-autonoetic-consciousness]]` (if exists), `[[topics/sleep-and-consciousness]]`, `[[topics/terminal-lucidity]]` (if exists), `[[topics/dissociative-disorders-and-consciousness]]`. See `reviews/optimistic-2026-05-18.md` §"Expansion Opportunities" High Priority.

### ✓ 2026-05-18: Write concept page on Discrimination Problem (consciousness epistemology)
- **Type**: expand-topic
- **Notes**: Suggested by optimistic-2026-05-18 (High Priority) and recommended in optimistic-2026-05-18 §"New Concept Pages Needed". Builds on §"Discrimination Problem" (lines 131–135) of `topics/consciousness-disruption-and-the-mind-brain-interface.md` which names an epistemological asymmetry — "we can prove consciousness is present...but we cannot prove it is absent" — that is genuinely original at the topic-article level and supplies a calibration constraint on every consciousness-attribution claim downstream. The principle recurs across the catalogue but lacks a canonical home: (i) animal-consciousness cluster (we can prove the octopus is doing X, we cannot prove it isn't conscious); (ii) AI-consciousness cluster (we can prove the model responds correctly to introspection prompts, we cannot prove it isn't a zombie); (iii) edge-of-sentience cases (`[[birch-edge-of-sentience-and-the-five-tier-scale]]`, foetuses, *Hydra*, minimal organisms); (iv) edge-states (`[[edge-states-and-void-probes]]`); (v) anaesthesia/DoC clinical evidence — CMD-style findings continuously revise the *prove-present* threshold downward without ever supplying a *prove-absent* upper bound. The concept page should (a) state the principle once cleanly — the asymmetry between operational prove-present and impossible prove-absent — and frame it as a structural feature of consciousness rather than a clinical inconvenience; (b) catalogue how the asymmetry operates differently across the four downstream cases above; (c) specify what kinds of evidence *would* count toward absence-claims (computational-architecture necessity arguments, anti-correlated metacognitive signal absence, the `[[apex/introspection-architecture-void-cluster]]` cluster's structural-criteria approach); (d) state how the asymmetry interacts with `[[evidential-status-discipline]]` — the absence-claim cannot be moved above *live hypothesis* by any combination of negative evidence; (e) honour `[[evidential-status-discipline]]` throughout (the discrimination-problem is itself a methodological commitment, not an empirical claim); (f) cross-link to `[[birch-edge-of-sentience-and-the-five-tier-scale]]`, `[[animal-consciousness]]`, `[[ai-consciousness]]`, `[[edge-states-and-void-probes]]`, `[[apophatic-cartography-four-criteria]]`, `[[evidential-status-discipline]]`. ### ✓ 2026-04-20: Write voids article on the Erasure Void
- **Type**: expand-topic
- **Notes**: Research completed in research/voids-erasure-void-2026-03-20.md (2026-03-20) and never synthesised into an article. Distinct from the inaccessible-past void (covers forgetting specific memories): the erasure void is about the deeper structural impossibility of auditing one's own cognitive completeness — consciousness cannot inventory its own deletions. Clinical anosognosia provides the starkest demonstration (Gertler; the 2024 TiCS review of visual metacognition failures identifying the three-step monitoring architecture; Alzheimer's three-form taxonomy — executive/mnemonic/primary), but the principle operates universally. Key sources in research note: Gertler on anosognosia and unity of consciousness, the TiCS 2024 visual-metacognition review, Alzheimer's metacognitive-error studies, the "unknown unknowns" / hypocognition material, and the SEP entry on epistemological problems of memory. Tenet alignment: Dualism (selective disruption of the monitoring interface is predicted by mind-brain distinctness but puzzling under identity theory), Bidirectional Interaction (self-monitoring has an architecture, not a brute given), Occam's Razor Has Limits (confabulation constructs the illusion of completeness). Category: Occluded/Unexplorable (mixed). Target section: voids/ (~93/100 — has capacity). Scope: 2200-2700 words. Cross-link candidates: [transparency-void](/voids/necessary-opacity/), [inaccessible-past](/voids/inaccessible-past/), [self-opacity](/voids/self-opacity/), [self-transcendence-void](/voids/self-transcendence-void/), [observation-void](/voids/observation-and-measurement-void/). Preserve distinction from inaccessible-past: this void is not about what has been forgotten but about the invisibility of the loss itself.
- **Output**: Write voids article on the Erasure Void

### ✓ 2026-03-17: Research Russellian monism as competitor to bi-aspectual dualism
- **Type**: research-topic
- **Notes**: Russellian monism (Chalmers 2015, Alter & Nagasawa 2015) is the closest competitor — both say physics describes structure while consciousness is "missing." Key differences to clarify: (1) Russellian monism is neutral monism (one substance, two aspects); the Map commits to genuine dualism. (2) Russellian monism typically implies panpsychism; the Map rejects it. (3) The combination problem hits Russellian monism hard; the Map's quantum-interface model may avoid it. (4) Does Russellian monism handle the measurement problem? Research Chalmers' "The Combination Problem for Panpsychism," Goff's "Consciousness and Fundamental Reality," Stoljar's "Ignorance and Imagination." Critical positioning work. Target: research note.
- **Output**: Russellian monism as competitor to bi-aspectual dualism

- **Notes**: Pessimistic review (2026-02-20 afternoon) found the article argues theoretical virtues malfunction for consciousness, then claims this is "predicted by dualism and anomalous for physicalism." ### P3: Concept page on the argument from mechanism (sufficiency-necessity non-sequitur)

Visual experience can be induced by direct cortical stimulation; that does not make ordinary vision hallucinatory"). The pattern is *portable*: it surfaces in psychedelic-experience debates (drug-induced mystical experience produces serotonergic cascade ↛ all mystical experience reduces to serotonergic cascade), in lucid-dreaming debates, in NDE debates, in dissociative-disorder debates, in religious-experience debates, and in many places where dualist-friendly phenomenology has a reductive sufficient-mechanism explanation available. A standalone concept page would (a) name the inferential pattern formally as a *sufficiency-vs-necessity* fallacy in the Map's named-discipline catalogue alongside `concepts/possibility-probability-slippage` and `concepts/evidential-status-discipline`; (b) catalogue the catalogue's existing instances (OBE, lucid dreaming, psychedelics, hypnagogic phenomenology) as worked examples; (c) develop the *symmetric* discipline — the materialist's argument from mechanism is rejected, but so is the dualist's argument from "no mechanism fully explains X therefore mind is involved", which is the parallel non-sequitur in the opposite direction; (d) install the article as a citable handle for dependent articles facing this inference-pattern. The Map already has the discipline operational across multiple articles; what is missing is the *named anchor* for it. Estimated scope: 1500–2000 words. Tenet alignment: methodological — interacts with Tenet 1 (the dualism-friendly inferences depend on the symmetric version of the discipline) and Tenet 5 (Occam's Razor Has Limits — premature parsimony is what the materialist's argument-from-mechanism move attempts). Hyperphantasia is mentioned in the body of the aphantasia article (line 47: "hyperphantasics describe imagery 'as vivid as real seeing' — indistinguishable, by their report, from perception in vividness if not in source-attribution") but is not explored at length. The asymmetry matters because the within-species-divergence wedge runs in *both* directions — the missing-content extreme and the extra-vividness extreme are both pressuring the same standard-imagery-vividness assumption. A hyperphantasia topic article would (a) deliver the lived report (Zeman's hyperphantasic case studies; the Simner work on prevalence and distribution); (b) develop the source-monitoring puzzle (the hyperphantasic's near-photographic imagery raises distinct reality-testing questions that aphantasia does not — link directly to the proposed source-attribution-divergence article); (c) engage the trauma/PTSD literature where imagery vividness becomes pathological (intrusive imagery; complex PTSD); (d) make the imagery-spectrum case symmetrical so the apex on within-species divergence has matched extremes rather than asymmetric coverage. Standard imagery rating instruments (VVIQ; OSIVQ; Plymouth Sensory Imagery Questionnaire) treat the spectrum as continuous; the topic articles should treat it that way too rather than only treating the missing-end pole. The hyperphantasia case is also where filter-theoretic readings face their hardest test: if vivid imagery were a candidate site for filter-leakage into the phenomenal field, hyperphantasics would be the population the framework predicts to find — frame as speculation per framework-stage-calibration discipline. Estimated scope: 2000–2500 words. Tenet alignment: Tenet 1 (Dualism), Tenet 5 (Occam's Razor Has Limits). Topics/ section at ~225/250 capacity — verify cap before placement. - **Type**: expand-topic

The despite-commitments / because-prediction split is doing a lot of work in the catalogue but its boundary cases are handled inline rather than systematically. A concept page would parse the boundary into three classes: (a) observation-and-framework-both-despite (Nisbett-Wilson 1977 — 1970s cognitivism did not predict the result; the field treated it as anomalous for a decade before absorbing it); (b) observation-despite-but-framework-developed-to-predict (Gazzaniga — the 1978 observation was despite-commitments; the 1985 interpreter framework was constructed to account for it; subsequent confirmations of the framework are because-prediction with respect to the framework itself); (c) observation-and-framework-both-because (Haidt social-intuitionist — moral judgement precedes rational justification was the prior commitment; the experimental confirmation was because-prediction throughout). The classification matters because the catalogue currently lumps (a) and (b) for headline-count purposes and the lumping inflates the count. Page should (a) state the three-class classification cleanly; (b) develop the classification against the present cluster's anchors; (c) audit one or two other clusters' anchors (e.g., the surplus-void's Wallace observation vs Chalmers's framework); (d) state what the three-class classification implies for the licensing-count discipline at the cluster level; (e) cross-link [common-cause-null](/project/common-cause-null/), [introspection-architecture-independence-scoring](/topics/introspection-architecture-independence-scoring/), [the-surplus-void](/voids/the-surplus-void/), [apophatic-cartography-four-criteria](/concepts/apophatic-cartography-four-criteria/).
